title: Senior Developer Marketing Manager, Lifecycle & Growth
descriptionPlain:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

The Developer Relations team builds developer tooling and creates awareness through events, social channels, and community activity. In this hands-on role, you’ll turn that attention into active users by owning the journey from first touch through signup, installation, first success, and continued engagement, while also owning the Developer Hub as the main conversion surface. By helping more developers discover and adopt 1Password’s developer tooling, you’ll contribute to the company’s mission and growth.

How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

What we're looking for:

• 4+ years of experience in developer marketing, lifecycle or customer relationship management (CRM) marketing, or growth marketing for a technical or developer-facing product.

• Proven experience building lifecycle programs that improved activation and retention, with measurable results.

• Hands-on experience with marketing automation and lifecycle tools such as Customer.io http://Customer.io, HubSpot, Braze, or Iterable, as well as product analytics tools such as Amplitude, Mixpanel, or PostHog.

• Experience owning or substantially improving website conversion performance, including A/B testing.

• Strong writing skills, with an instinct for what developers find useful and credible.

• Comfort working with engineers and developer advocates and with technical concepts such as application programming interfaces (APIs), command-line interfaces (CLIs), software development kits (SDKs), and documentation. You do not need to be a developer, but you should be able to try the product yourself.

• Ability to work independently and communicate clearly in a remote, async-friendly team. Preferred: Experience with product-led growth, free-to-paid conversion, open source adoption, event and community programs, Structured Query Language (SQL), Hypertext Markup Language (HTML), Cascading Style Sheets (CSS), scripting, search engine optimization (SEO), docs-led growth, or developer communities such as GitHub, Discord, Reddit, Hacker News, X, or LinkedIn.

What you can expect:

• Build capture-to-activation flows for leads from conferences, meetups, hackathons, webinars, and social channels, including QR codes, event-specific landing pages, follow-up sequences, and starter kits.

• Work with Developer Relations teammates so every event, talk, and social moment has a clear call to action, tracking, and post-event nurture plan.

• Turn social engagement, including launches, threads, demos, and community moments, into measurable traffic and signups through the right landing pages and offers.

• Design and run lifecycle programs across onboarding, activation, adoption, re-engagement, and expansion using email, in-product messaging, and community channels.

• Define activation for the product, build programs around milestones such as a first application programming interface (API) call, successful build, or integration, and segment messaging by behavior, role, language, technology stack, and source.

• Own the Developer Hub’s strategy, messaging, and conversion across its homepage, product pages, community pages, and events pages. Run continuous testing across copy, calls to action, page structure, and signup flows, and partner with Design, Engineering, and Documentation to improve time-to-first-value.

• Write or direct tutorials, quickstarts, sample applications, changelogs, and email content; build reporting from first touch through activation and retention; and share findings that help shape the roadmap and messaging. Early success will include auditing the funnel, launching event follow-up and onboarding programs, and improving signup-to-activation, event-to-user, and Developer Hub conversion.

USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $133,000 USD and $186,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $125,000 CAD and $175,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Our culture
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results.

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

Our approach to remote work
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events.

What we offer
We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer:

Health and wellbeing
👶 Maternity and parental leave top-up programs
🩺 Competitive health benefits
🏝 Generous PTO policy

 Growth and future
📈 RSU program for most employees
💸 Retirement matching program
🔑 Free 1Password account

Community
🤝 Paid volunteer days
🏆 Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly
🌎 Remote-first work environment
*Some roles in our GTM team are currently being hired for in-person hybrid work in Toronto and Austin. These roles will specify on the posting.

You belong here.

1Password is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Be yourself, find your people and share the things you love.

Accommodation is available upon request at any point during our recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please speak to your talent acquisition partner or email us at nextbit@agilebits.com and we’ll work to meet your needs.

Remote work is a part of our DNA. Given that our company was founded remotely in 2005, we can safely say we're experts at building remote culture. That said, remote work at 1Password does mean working from your home country. If you've got questions or concerns about this, your talent partner would be happy to address them with you.

Successful applicants will be required to complete a background check that may consist of prior employment verification, reference checks, education confirmation, criminal background, publicly available social media, credit history, or other information, as permitted by local law.

1Password uses artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technologies, including natural language processing and predictive analytics, to assist in the initial screening of employment applications and improve our recruitment process. See here https://www.ashbyhq.com/downloadables/ashby-bias-audit-08-2024.pdf for the latest third party bias audit information. If you prefer not to have your application assessed using AI/ML features, you may opt out by completing this form https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/1password/automation-notice. For additional information see our Candidate Privacy Notice https://1password.com/files/candidate-privacy-notice.pdf.

As a Enterprise Account Executive, you will own a focused territory of strategic target accounts and existing customers with 2,501+ employees, with an emphasis on Fortune 100 and Global 2000 organizations. Your mandate is to create new executive relationships, build qualified pipeline, win complex multi-million-dollar platform opportunities, and expand 1Password’s strategic footprint across an existing book of business.

This is not a transactional or single-product sales role. You will lead an enterprise-wide security conversation, starting with a customer’s most urgent problem and building the strategic case for Unified Access across humans, AI agents, and machines. You will engage and multi-thread with CISOs, CIOs, IT and security leaders, IAM teams, DevOps and platform teams, engineering leaders, security architects, finance, procurement, and other executive stakeholders.

The Enterprise Account Executive role also requires experience selling to financial-services organizations headquartered in or operating from New York City. You will bring an active network, sector fluency, and a demonstrated understanding of how to navigate and win within complex financial institutions.

How we’re using AI today
Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.

Expectations of this role

This is a field-based sales role. That means you are expected to be regularly engaged in customer-facing activities, including in-person meetings, events, and other travel as required to effectively support your territory. Territory locations that are preferable for this role are:

Candidates must be based in the New York metro area , Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Boston or Washington DC area and should expect regular in-person customer meetings, industry events, and travel throughout the territory, including travel to New York City as required.

Your primary work location will be your home office, but your role requires a lot of mobility and flexibility. Travel within your assigned territory, and occasionally outside of it, will be a part of your job, and you are responsible for managing your schedule in a way that works for the company and you.

Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto.

What we're looking for:

 - 10+ years of successful enterprise cybersecurity sales experience, including substantial experience selling to Fortune 100 or Global 2000 organizations.

 - A consistent record of exceeding $2M+ annual quotas, including experience carrying quotas in the $2M–$5M+ range and closing complex, multi-million-dollar opportunities.

 - Multiple years of elite sales performance and company recognition, such as President’s Club or equivalent top-performer awards.

 - Demonstrated success selling enterprise platforms and multi-product transformations, not only transactional or stand-alone point products.

 - Experience selling Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions, with a strong understanding of identity security, AI and Machine identity risks,  Zero Trust, cloud security, developer security, or adjacent cybersecurity platforms.

 - Established, credible relationships with enterprise CISOs, CIOs, senior security and IT leaders, IAM leaders, and identity/security architects within the territory or relevant named-account segment.

 - Proven ability to engage IAM, IT security, DevOps, platform engineering, and engineering leaders and connect their technical priorities to an executive business case.

 - A record of winning net-new strategic logos and expanding existing accounts through cross-sell, upsell, and multi-year platform agreements.

 - Strong executive presence and the ability to communicate credibly with C-suite leaders and deeply technical audiences.

 - Rigorous account planning, pipeline creation, opportunity management, forecasting, and negotiation skills.

NEW YORK FINANCIAL-SERVICES EXPERTISE

 - Significant experience selling complex cybersecurity platforms to major banks, capital-markets firms, insurers, asset managers, fintech companies, or other financial institutions headquartered in or operating from New York City.

 - An active, credible network of CISO, CIO, CTO, security, identity, infrastructure, cloud, engineering, architecture, risk, and procurement leaders within New York financial-services accounts, relationships you can confidently activate to open strategic conversations.

 - Deep familiarity with financial-services buying cycles, including security and architecture review, third-party risk management, regulatory and compliance requirements, procurement, legal review, testing, implementation planning, and executive approval.

 - Working knowledge of the technology stacks and infrastructure common to large financial institutions, including hybrid and multi-cloud environments, identity and privileged-access systems, endpoint controls, developer platforms, legacy infrastructure, and highly regulated production environments.

 - A demonstrated record of mapping complex stakeholder groups, building internal consensus, navigating incumbents and competitive dynamics, and winning large, multi-year cybersecurity agreements within New York financial-services accounts.

What you can expect:

OWN AND GROW A STRATEGIC ENTERPRISE TERRITORY

 - Develop and execute sophisticated account and territory plans for a focused portfolio of high-value prospects and customers.

 - Create new executive relationships while using your established network among CISOs, CIOs, identity leaders, security architects, and other senior technology buyers to accelerate access and credibility.

 - Identify whitespace, competitive displacement opportunities, and compelling events across identity security, AI adoption, privileged access, SaaS governance, developer workflows, and device security.

 - Build and maintain the pipeline coverage, account engagement, and deal velocity required to consistently achieve or exceed a significant annual quota.

SELL THE FULL PLATFORM STORY

 - Elevate conversations from an individual point-product need to a strategic Unified Access vision spanning people, AI agents, and machines.

 - Connect 1Password’s capabilities to measurable outcomes, including reducing credential and access risk, eliminating standing privilege, governing SaaS and shadow AI, protecting developer and machine workflows, strengthening device trust, and improving auditability.

 - Land with the customer’s most urgent use case, then build an executive-backed roadmap for adoption and expansion across Enterprise Password Manager, SaaS Manager, Credential Broker, Device Trust, and Privileged Access.

 - Translate complex identity, access, cloud, endpoint, developer, and AI-security concepts into clear business value for executive and deeply technical audiences.

LEAD COMPLEX, MULTI-STAKEHOLDER SALES CYCLES

 - Orchestrate 6–12+ month enterprise sales cycles involving security, IAM, IT, DevOps, platform engineering, application engineering, finance, legal, procurement, and executive sponsors.

 - Build consensus across large buying groups and establish clear business, technical, economic, and decision criteria.

 - Lead executive presentations, discovery sessions, workshops, business-value assessments, commercial negotiations, and close plans.

 - Create and maintain mutual action plans and apply MEDDPPICC or a comparable enterprise qualification methodology with discipline.

 - Structure and negotiate complex, multi-year, multi-product agreements with material ARR and platform expansion potential.

EXPAND STRATEGIC CUSTOMER RELATIONSHIPS

 - Build broad, durable relationships throughout customer organizations rather than relying on a single champion.

 - Uncover business and security priorities beyond the initial use case and turn them into platform expansion opportunities.

 - Partner with Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, product specialists, and services teams to create adoption and expansion plans tied to measurable outcomes.

OPERATE AS ONE TEAM

 - Collaborate closely with BDR, Solutions Engineering, Channels, Alliances, Customer Success, Onboarding, Product, Marketing, Legal, and Deal Desk.

 - Co-sell with strategic partners, cloud alliances, channel teams, and systems integrators where they can expand reach or accelerate a decision.

 - Represent 1Password at executive briefings, customer meetings, trade shows, and industry events.

 - Maintain accurate opportunity data, next steps, forecasts, and account plans in Salesforce.

 - Use AI and modern selling tools thoughtfully to improve research, preparation, coaching, and execution while creating more time for customer engagement.

Bonus points for:

 - Experience competing and winning against major enterprise identity and cybersecurity platform providers.

 - Deep knowledge of identity and access management, privileged access management, credential security, machine identities, agentic AI security, SaaS governance, device trust, or secrets management.

 - Proficiency with MEDDPPICC, Salesforce, Slack, Zoom, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Outreach, and AI-enabled sales tools.

 - Experience developing opportunities through channel partners, cloud alliances, systems integrators, or technology partners.

How you work:

 - You create a compelling platform narrative while keeping the customer’s priorities, maturity, and path to value at the center.

 - You combine strategic thinking with operating rigor; your account plans, pipeline, forecasts, and close plans are current, specific, and dependable.

 - You are resilient, accountable, collaborative, and motivated by ambitious targets and complex opportunities.

 - You are coachable, apply feedback quickly, and continuously improve your craft.

 - You thrive in a remote, field-based environment and prioritize meaningful in-person customer engagement.

 - You lead with curiosity and strong discovery, uncovering the broader security and business problem rather than stopping at the initial product request.

title: Training Specialist, Welding (FX)
descriptionPlain:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Training Specialist - Welding owns welding training at their site. You will teach technicians to weld to a written standard across TIG, MIG and mechanized processes, run the evaluations that confirm they are ready, and keep the training records and documentation that the program is audited against. The role works closely with our naval customer as a representative of Hadrian.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You will report to the site Training Operations Manager, with a dotted line to our welding training lead, who sets the welding curriculum and standard. You will set your own course with minimal oversight, direct trainees day to day without managing them, and make recommendations to leadership when the program needs them.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

You will lead welding training at your site, delivering hands-on instruction in the booth and on the floor and acting as the technical expert for the technicians you train. You will bring technicians to weld to the written standard across TIG, MIG and mechanized welding, with consistent execution across every shift, and you will learn new processes and methods as they are introduced and turn them into clear, teachable steps.

You will own the evaluation process, including weld tests, practical assessments, quizzes, progress reporting and evaluation criteria across hard and soft skills. You will record training, evaluations and qualifications in our training software so records are complete and current, and you will maintain version-controlled, audit-ready welding training documentation and conduct training audits for procedural compliance.

You will develop and refine welding curriculum with our welding training lead, adapting the core training system to your site. You will give trainees day-to-day direction and escalate performance concerns to the Training Operations Manager, and you will carry Hadrian's standards and culture into your work with our naval customer.

WHAT YOU BRING

Required

 - Experience in multiple welding disciplines, including TIG (GTAW), MIG (GMAW) and mechanized welding

 - 3+ years in a training, instructing or teaching role focused on entry-level individual contributors

 - At least 1 year welding in a production environment

 - Proven ability to train people from entry level to mid level to weld to a written standard

 - Openness to learning new processes and methods, and to reteaching as they change

 - Comfort working with software to record training, evaluations and qualifications

 - Experience maintaining training documentation to an audit-ready standard

 - Ability to recognize patterns in how people learn and give objective, actionable recommendations to leadership

 - A self-starter who manages their own time and priorities with minimal oversight

 - Willingness to travel around 25%, primarily to our Los Angeles facility for training purposes

Preferred, not necessary

 - Experience welding or training to NAVSEA standards

 - Experience with robotic welding; this can be learned and trained in role

 - Welding certifications such as AWS Certified Welder, Certified Welding Educator or Certified Welding Inspector

 - Experience building welding curriculum or training documentation from the ground up

 - Ability to influence without direct authority

 - Comfort representing a company in front of a customer

 - High emotional intelligence; improves on feedback and coaches others

 - Passion for training, career development and Hadrian's mission of reindustrializing the nation's workforce

OUR VALUES

 - Surgical Precision: welds, evaluations, records and documentation have to be exact.

 - Own the Outcome: you own the training outcome at your site and meet the intent of the standard.

 - Build, Edit, Scale: our welding curriculum is moving from pilot to scale, and you will help refine it.

COMPENSATION

For this role, the target salary range is $27 - $45 per hour (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees
   401k

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need.

 - Flexible vacation policy

 - Equity

 

ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 

USE OF AI IN HIRING

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy https://www.hadrian.co/privacy-policy.

 

CONSIDERATION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

 

HADRIAN IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

 - Partner with procurement and operations on advanced supply chain strategies including long-term purchasing and strategic safety stock.

 - Proactively manage inventory to prevent stock-outs and own allocation of constrained supply.

 - Analyze supply chain data and report on MRP health metrics relative to factory production goals and delivery commitments.

 - Own the leadership communication on the program to all key stakeholders: program management, operations, engineering & supply chain.

 - Proactively update operations leadership and engineering on critical supply issues requiring escalation.

 - Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, operations, engineering, or a related field

 - 3+ years of experience in material program management, material planning, production planning, supply chain management, purchasing, or operations.

 - Track record supporting material planning for new product introduction (NPI) from prototype through rate production

 - Experience working within MRP or ERP systems

 - Strong analytical skills; comfortable working with data to drive supply planning decisions

 - Excellent written and verbal communication; able to escalate supply risks clearly to cross-functional stakeholders

 - Detail-oriented, self-motivated, and able to respond quickly in a fast-moving, ever-changing environment

 - Experience navigating multi-tier BOMs and complex work orders in a high-mix manufacturing environment

Hadrian’s contracting function is scaling alongside its factories. This seat will help design the workflows, systems, and controls that move agreements from intake to signature across sales and procurement, and is measured on the cycle time it removes.

This seat negotiates and administers those customer agreements, including long-term supply agreements, master agreements, customer purchase orders, and Hadrian’s quote terms. Many arrive carrying FAR, DFARS, export control, and data rights requirements from the prime contract. The seat confirms Hadrian can perform them and flows them correctly

 - Scaling Hadrian’s manufacturing footprint requires the purchase of machine tools, automation cells, raw material, castings and forgings, outside processing, tooling, and software. This seat owns Hadrian’s purchase order terms and the category addenda supporting them, adjudicates supplier markups, and serves as the contracts partner to Supply Chain and Procurement into its supply base.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own assigned customer and supplier agreements from intake through closeout: pre-award review, negotiation, award, acceptance, performance, modification, renewal, and closeout. Administer Hadrian’s subcontracts under prime contractor terms. Track deliverables, milestones, acceptance, and notice dates against each contract, and escalate noncompliance before it becomes a dispute.

 - Draft, revise, and interpret long-term supply agreements, master agreements, subcontracts, purchase orders, quote terms, non-disclosure agreements, statements of work, amendments, and change orders. Produce clear, defensible language on Hadrian’s paper and precise redlines on the counterparty’s.

 - Digest the FAR, DFARS, and customer-specific clauses the primes flow down to Hadrian through customer agreements and purchase orders. Determine which obligations Hadrian must carry, which must flow to its suppliers, and which do not apply. Apply them to the correct vendor agreements order by order and maintain the record of which clauses attached where. Challenge flowdowns that exceed what the prime contract requires or what a commercial supplier should reasonably accept.

 - Draft and administer Hadrian’s terms for subcontracts, suppliers, and capital equipment, including acceptance, warranty, title and risk of loss, and milestone payment structures. Verify that the correct Hadrian terms and category addenda attach to every order, screen order-face fields for the completeness downstream controls depend on, and confirm order terms do not conflict with the governing master agreement

 - Review customer terms, purchase orders, and long-term agreements from the primes against Hadrian’s established positions, and identify the pricing, liability, intellectual property, and data rights terms that require escalation. Adjudicate markups returned against Hadrian’s purchase order and quote terms under the playbook, and determine acceptance within delegated authority. Prepare the response setting out Hadrian’s position in terms the counterparty can act on.

 - Own the portfolio end to end across customers, suppliers, and prospective partners. Apply the review checklist to every inbound form, issue Hadrian’s standard redline, and distribute Hadrian’s form on request. Determine whether a mutual or unilateral instrument is appropriate and which party is protected. Approve deviations within the playbook, negotiate to closure, and track expirations.

 - Maintain the contract record in accordance with company and regulatory requirements. Define and enforce the contract file standard and naming conventions, own the central repository, and administer records retention. Drive discovery and reconciliation of legacy agreements to completion.

 - Bachelor’s degree in business administration, contracts management, supply chain management, finance, law, or a related field.

 - 5+ years in contract management, contract administration, or procurement contracting in aerospace, defense, or advanced manufacturing, including full lifecycle responsibility for customer and supplier agreements personally negotiated and administered.

 - Experience negotiating from the supplier’s side of the table with prime contractors or major OEMs, including long-term supply agreements, customer terms and purchase orders, and the pricing, delivery, and liability commitments behind them

 - Substantial experience administering purchase orders, supplier terms, and subcontracts in a manufacturing, industrial, or hardware environment, including capital equipment or major asset purchases and the acceptance, installation, and milestone payment structures behind them.

 - Working command of the FAR and DFARS clauses primes flow down to their suppliers. The candidate understands how prime-tier subcontracts and purchase orders are formed, administered, and modified, and how the prime’s contract type shapes the terms it flows down.

 - Demonstrated record of negotiating complex agreements to closure across price, terms, schedule, and risk allocation. The candidate has authored language issued under their organization’s name, not solely revised the work of others, across supply agreements, master agreements, basic ordering agreements, subcontracts, purchase orders, non-disclosure agreements, change orders, and license agreements.

The Construction Quality Assurance Manager will work directly with Hadrian’s project team to provide field-level quality oversight of construction activities and will coordinate closely with the General Contractor, subcontractors, design engineers, third-party testing and inspection agencies, commissioning personnel, and equipment teams.

This is an owner-side quality assurance role. The Construction Quality Assurance Manager will independently verify that appropriate quality control processes are being implemented, construction complies with project requirements, required testing and inspections are performed, and identified deficiencies are properly resolved.

The successful candidate will be highly field-oriented and capable of identifying quality risks before they affect downstream construction, equipment installation, commissioning, manufacturing operations, cost, or schedule.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Construction Quality Assurance Program

 - Develop, implement, and maintain Hadrian’s project-specific Construction Quality Assurance Plan.

 - Establish quality assurance processes, documentation requirements, inspection protocols, and acceptance criteria across construction scopes.

 - Review the General Contractor’s project-specific Quality Control Plan and verify that appropriate QC processes are being implemented in the field.

 - Establish clear responsibilities between Hadrian, the General Contractor, subcontractors, design engineers, and third-party testing and inspection agencies.

 - Review and monitor Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs) for critical construction activities.

 - Establish appropriate hold points, witness points, inspection requirements, and documentation requirements for critical work.

 - Identify high-risk construction activities and establish appropriate quality oversight before work begins.

 - Promote a proactive quality program focused on preventing defects rather than identifying problems after installation.

 - Work directly with Hadrian Field Engineers and Superintendent to identify potential quality issues and verify compliance with project requirements.

 - Monitor workmanship and installation quality across civil, structural, architectural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, process utility, and equipment-support scopes.

 - Establish and manage the project process for identifying, documenting, tracking, and closing construction deficiencies and Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs).

 - Verify critical work prior to concealment, concrete placement, equipment installation, energization, startup, or turnover as applicable.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Hadrian is building an additive manufacturing capability that runs as part of an autonomous factory, not as a room full of printers. The hard problem is not any single machine, material, or line of code. It is making all of them behave as one system. Systems engineering is the glue that holds that system together, and this role owns the glue.

The Senior Director leads three engineering functions, materials and process engineering, hardware engineering, and software engineering, and is accountable for the digital backbone that binds them to each other and to applications engineering: the architecture, interfaces, and data that connect Hadrian’s Opus platform to cutting-edge additive manufacturing equipment, add automation where it makes sense, fuse sensor data into the part record, and turn a collection of parts into a full, integrated digital manufacturing system built around additive.

The measure of success is not three strong teams. It is one manufacturing system that a customer part flows through, from design intent to qualified hardware, with every decision and every data point captured along the way.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Architect the system. Define and control the end-to-end architecture for additive at Hadrian: requirements, interfaces, data model, and acceptance criteria that hold across multiple equipment platforms, modalities, and sites. Treat the factory as the product.

 - Build the digital backbone. Connect additive equipment, peripherals, and inspection assets to Opus with the same discipline a semiconductor fab applies to connecting tools to the host: standardized state models, telemetry, event streams, and data contracts, with security and configuration control built in.

 - Fuse the sensors. Bring in-situ monitoring, machine telemetry, environmental data, and downstream inspection into one correlated record per part, then move from monitoring to data-driven release and, where it is justified, closed-loop control.

 - Automate where it pays. Lead automation across additive cells (material and powder handling, build changeover, part removal and depowdering, post-processing flow, robotics, controls, and safety) with a written case for each: safety, repeatability, and data capture first; labor second. Never automate an unstable process.

 - Lead the three functions as one. Set standards, priorities, and cadence for materials and process, hardware, and software engineering. Resolve conflicts between them at the architecture level, not the escalation level.

 - Own the applications engineering interface. With the Head of Applications Engineering, define what a production-ready hand-off looks like, publish the process capability and design-rule data applications engineers build to, and close the loop from floor results back into design guidance.

 - Industrialize the equipment. Through the hardware engineering leader, own factory and site acceptance, commissioning, reliability (preventive maintenance, spares, MTBF/MTTR), and configuration-controlled modification and upgrade of additive systems, and lead the technical relationships with equipment partners that unlock deeper integration. The machine-level depth lives in that team; the standards and the outcomes live here.

 - Design for the factory. Partner with Factory Development and Factory Automation on cell and site design: material flow, capacity, simulation, utilities, and the path to lights-out operation for additive.

 - Build quality in. Make the system itself the evidence: traceability, data integrity, and process control that stand up to AS9100 audits and customer qualification without a separate paper trail.

 - Be the additive voice in Hadrian’s platform. Carry additive requirements into Core Engineering and the Opus roadmap, and bring platform capability back to the floor.

 - Hire, develop, and retain. Build a leadership bench under you, set a high technical bar, and make Hadrian the place the best additive systems engineers in the country want to work.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a physical science; an advanced degree is strongly preferred.

 - 12+ years in advanced manufacturing, with real depth in at least three of these six domains: factory design and industrial automation; semiconductor or other high-reliability capital-equipment engineering; manufacturing software and data systems; materials science and process engineering; quality systems in regulated industries; sensing, process monitoring, and sensor fusion.

 - 5+ years leading engineering teams, including leading through managers and building at least one function from the ground up.

 - Production experience with metal laser powder bed fusion, as a user of the equipment, a developer of it, or both.

 - Has led the integration of complex equipment into factory-level software (manufacturing execution, equipment host, or data platforms), including requirements, interface standards, and acceptance criteria.

 - Has taken at least one production automation or capital-equipment program (robotic cells, material handling, or equipment with safety systems and controls) from concept through commissioning in a regulated environment (aerospace and defense, semiconductor, medical, or similar), and has owned the reliability of production equipment afterward.

 - Fluent across the stack: can review a process flow, a data schema, a metallurgical cross-section, and a controls narrative in the same meeting, and knows which one is lying.

 - Has worked as a true peer to a customer-facing or design function, with a record of building clean interfaces rather than absorbing the other team.

 - Willing to travel up to 20%, including to Hadrian sites and international partners. Must meet the ITAR requirements below.

WHAT WILL SET YOU APART

 - Ph.D. in materials science, mechanical engineering, systems engineering or a related discipline.

 - Semiconductor capital-equipment background: equipment-to-host integration, tool matching, fleet data, fault detection and statistical process control at scale.

 - Equipment-maker experience developing or launching metal additive systems (new product introduction, cost-productivity trades, design reviews) in addition to user-side experience.

 - In-situ monitoring and sensor fusion implemented in production, with data-driven release or closed-loop control.

 - Factory design: material flow planning, discrete-event simulation, and highly automated or lights-out operations.

 - AS9100 and customer qualification pathways; familiarity with AM specifications (ASTM F42, ISO/ASTM 529xx, SAE AMS 7xxx series).

 - Budget or P&L ownership of a capital-intensive program, with a record of making the build-versus-buy and automate-versus-wait calls well.

 - Modern software fluency: APIs, event streaming, OT/IT architecture, industrial interoperability standards (OPC UA, MTConnect), and cloud data platforms.

This role is ideal for an experienced in-house or real estate lawyer who is comfortable being an individual contributor and has managed and advised on complex, high-value industrial and commercial transactions.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Act as the primary legal owner for Hadrian’s real estate portfolio, including industrial, manufacturing, office, and R&D facilities.

 - Structure, draft, and negotiate complex real estate deals, including:

   - Industrial and office leases, subleases, amendments, and renewals

   - Purchase and sale agreements, options, and rights of first refusal/offer

   - Construction, design-build, architect, and general contractor agreements

 - Lead legal diligence and coordinate with senior leaders on site selection and evaluation, including overseeing environmental reviews and permitting

 - Advise on economic development incentives, tax abatements, grants, and public-private partnerships with state and local governments

 - Work with Strategy and Operations on landlord relations, operating covenants, tenant improvements, and lease administration

 - Identify and manage risks specific to manufacturing sites, such as environmental, hazardous materials, utilities and power, and security requirements for regulated or defense-related facilities

 - Manage and direct outside counsel, brokers, and consultants while keeping quality high and costs under control

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - JD from an accredited law school and active bar membership in at least one U.S. jurisdiction

 - 7–10+ years of real estate experience, including at a top law firm or in-house

 - Deep experience with commercial and industrial leasing and development or construction deals

 - Proven ability to lead complex, high-value deals from start to finish with little oversight

 - Strong business judgment and ability to weigh legal risk against need for execution

WHAT WILL SET YOU APART

 - Experience supporting manufacturing, industrial, energy, data center, or other heavy-infrastructure real estate

 - Experience with multi-state site selection and rapid portfolio growth at a high-growth company

 - Experience with drafting and negotiating agreements based on AIA or similar forms

 - Familiarity with environmental law, land use, and permitting for industrial sites

 - Exposure to real estate requirements for defense, government, or other regulated facilities

 - Experience building real estate legal processes and lease management systems from scratch

COMPENSATION

For this role, the target salary range is $200,000-  $285,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. Notion is shaping the future of Go-To-Market, and as a Solutions Consultant (SC), you’ll bring that future to life by building alongside customers and turning their biggest challenges into measurable outcomes. As a customer-facing, quota-carrying SC, you’ll bring together technical fluency and commercial ownership to grow your book of business. You’ll build pipeline with BDRs, engage key stakeholders, lead discovery, co-build workflow solutions live with customers, and guide opportunities through close. You’ll connect each solution to a clear business case and stay engaged through adoption, expansion, and renewal so customers realize the value of what they buy.

You’ll partner with BDRs, Outcomes Architects, and technical or product specialists while maintaining clear ownership of customer relationships, opportunity momentum, and next steps. If you’re a builder who loves to sell—and want to work at the intersection of AI, productivity, and enterprise—this is the role.

 

WHAT YOU’LL ACHIEVE

 - Create pipeline across your book of business. Build target-account plans with BDRs and initiate outreach to priority stakeholders to generate qualified opportunities, alongside BDR-sourced pipeline.

 - Own opportunities from first conversation through close. Lead discovery, qualify business needs and urgency, align stakeholders, shape the solution and business case, and drive the evaluation and commercial decision. Navigate commercial sizing, proposal construction, procurement, legal, and security review to close deals with the right scope, credits, and implementation path.

 - Design and validate workflow solutions that deliver measurable value. Map current- and future-state workflows, co-build solutions live in Notion, and define realistic scope, success criteria, and an implementation path. Translate customer needs and validated outcomes into a clear business case, commercial recommendation, and decision path. Treat discovery as an opportunity to build and validate.

 - Orchestrate the right partners while maintaining ownership. Engage BDRs, Outcomes Architects, and technical or product specialists at the right moments, with clear context and asks, while owning opportunity momentum, customer communication, and next steps.

 - Drive customer value and commercial growth after signature. Partner with Outcomes Architects, guide the initial path to value with a clear adoption plan, on onboarding and ongoing multi-workflow adoption, and own expansion strategy and renewal planning. Stay accountable for translating credits sold into credits consumed, and surface risks or expansion opportunities as customer workflows mature.

 

SKILLS YOU’LL NEED TO BRING

 - Mid-market sales experience. You have experience selling technical products to technical buyers at mid-market organizations (500–2,999 employees).

 - Commercial ownership and pipeline generation. You can demonstrate how you created or advanced business, influenced customer decisions, and owned measurable outcomes. Relevant experience may come from quota-carrying sales or adjacent customer-facing roles.

 - Technical fluency and builder mindset. You are comfortable building live in software and can demo, co-design, and troubleshoot with a customer without needing a specialist in the room.

 - AI fluency. You are excited about AI, build with new tools, and continually learn new ways of working.

 - Discovery, qualification, and value articulation. You can uncover customer needs, map workflows, qualify business impact and urgency, and translate what you learn into commercial outcomes, adoption plans, and clear success criteria.

 - Agency, urgency, and learning velocity. You set clear goals, take initiative, learn from customer interactions, and apply those learnings to improve outcomes. You bring new ideas and workflows to customers and make complex problems easier to solve.

 - Complex customer engagement. You can lead multi-stakeholder interactions and navigate procurement, legal, and security review cycles.

 - Native or bilingual-level Korean fluency and business-level English proficiency

 

NICE TO HAVES

 - Full-cycle B2B software sales experience or solutions engineering experience, with a consistent track record of exceeding quota across new-logo acquisition and expansion motions.

   - Familiarity with usage-based or consumption-based pricing models and the ability to structure credit-based commercial proposals.

 - Prior experience selling to mid-market accounts in productivity, collaboration, or workflow software.

 - Experience in a shared account ownership model, partnering with a post-sale or Customer Success team as part of an integrated customer motion.

We're looking for a senior brand campaign leader who can set the vision for our biggest moments, turn ambiguous business goals into breakthrough campaign strategy, and rally a lean, cross-functional team to deliver work that's both culturally relevant and commercially effective.

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

The Campaign Lead, Brand owns the strategy, orchestration, and performance of Notion's largest integrated brand campaigns—the tentpole moments that tell the most important stories about who we are, what we make, and why it matters. You'll be the connective tissue across launches and campaigns, making sure every global brand moment brings a cohesive, inspiring narrative to market across channels, audiences, and regions.

Reporting to the Head of Brand & Integrated Marketing, you'll set the brand campaign roadmap, lead campaigns end-to-end from first brief to performance readout, and raise the bar for how the team plans, builds, and learns. You'll partner closely with Product Marketing, Creative, Comms, Growth Marketing, and Regional Marketing leads, and help develop other campaign managers on the team. Responsibilities include:

 - Define and own the annual brand campaign roadmap, aligning tentpole moments to company priorities, product launches, and business goals

 - Lead Notion's largest cross-functional tentpole campaigns from strategy through execution and measurement, making high-stakes calls on concept, channel mix, and trade-offs

 - Partner with in-house Creative to originate and champion bold, category-defining brand concepts, and know when to push an idea further versus when to ship it

 - Partner with Product Marketing and Comms to unify product and brand narratives into a single, compelling story for each moment

 - Own campaign budgets and agency/vendor relationships, and partner with Growth Marketing on integrated brand and performance media from planning through reporting

 - Build the measurement framework for brand campaigns with Analytics and Growth, connecting awareness and consideration to pipeline and business outcomes

 - Collaborate with regional teams and localization to adapt and scale campaigns across EMEA, APAC, and other key markets

 - Evolve the campaign operating system—briefs, tiering, workback plans, retros, and AI-powered workflows—so the whole team moves faster with more clarity

 - Represent brand campaigns with marketing leadership and executives, presenting strategy, progress, and results with a clear point of view

SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING:

 - 12+ years of experience in integrated or brand marketing, preferably in AI or tech, with a track record of leading large-scale, multi-channel brand campaigns that moved the business

 - Idea catalyst: You bring a concept-led approach and an opinionated point of view, sparking, shaping, and shepherding breakthrough concepts until they're undeniable—and you can sell them up and across the org

 - Strategic owner: You turn ambiguous goals into a clear campaign strategy and roadmap, and you're comfortable owning outcomes, budget, and trade-offs end to end

 - Hybrid brand + performance thinker: You care about craft and tone, and you think rigorously about metrics, media, and sales enablement. You're not a purist in any one discipline

 - AI fluency: You have deep, first-hand experience experimenting with AI tools and agents, and you have a perspective on the balance of human vs. AI in creative generation

 - Speed: You bias toward action and operate with ambition, creating processes that help cross-functional teams do the same

 - Leader without the title: People on the projects you lead become the best versions of themselves by working with you. You influence senior stakeholders, navigate conflicting feedback, and level up the people around you

 - Order agent: You possess strong organizational and analytical skills, with the ability to run multiple complex workstreams at once while iterating for improvement

NICE TO HAVES:

 - Experience leading global and/or regionalized campaigns

 - Experience managing creative agencies and large media budgets

 - Familiarity with hybrid audience targeting (individuals, teams, and enterprise)

 - Experience mentoring or managing marketers

 - Experience using Notion—both personally and professionally

title: Software Engineer, Presence
descriptionPlain:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Presence is OpenAI’s team building AI agents that organizations can trust to handle real conversations and get things done. Our mission is to turn advances in frontier models into dependable systems that can resolve customer issues, support employees, and improve through experience in production.

Imagine calling about an unexpected charge. An agent needs to understand your situation, verify your identity, find the relevant account information, apply the right policy, and resolve the issue or bring in a person. It needs to do all of this naturally, accurately, and quickly, even when the conversation takes an unexpected turn. Presence brings together the models, execution systems, integrations, and controls that make experiences like this possible across voice, chat and email.

One of our most exciting challenges is what happens after an agent goes live. We're building a system for understanding where agents fail and making them better: investigate a production conversation, reproduce the problem in an evaluation, use Codex to develop a fix, test it against the current agent, and measure the result after deployment. Our ambition is to make more of this improvement process agentic over time, while giving people control over what changes reach users.

Read the launch announcement https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/.

 

WHAT WE WORK ON

 - Realtime voice: Natural conversations with fast responses, interruptions, and reliable audio, even under heavy traffic.

 - Agent systems: Orchestration, reasoning, tool execution, integrations with company systems, and enforcing permissions and policies.

 - Agent quality: Production debugging, simulations, evaluation infrastructure, regression testing, and measuring whether changes improve real outcomes.

 - Product and developer experience: Making it easier for teams to build, test, deploy, and operate sophisticated agents using Codex and OpenAI's capabilities.

 

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

You'll work at the intersection of frontier research, product engineering, and production systems, with a direct feedback loop from people using what you build. We collaborate closely with Research, Forward Deployed Engineers, and customers to understand where models and systems break down and turn those lessons into improvements that can benefit many deployments.

The impact is already tangible. At launch, Presence was resolving 75% of issues coming into OpenAI's English phone support without a human, and its Codex-assisted improvement process helped cut transfers to people by 15 percentage points over ten days. Introducing OpenAI Presence https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/

We're looking for people excited by ambitious engineering problems, building products people depend on, and helping define how AI agents are developed and improved in the real world.

 

YOUR BACKGROUND MIGHT LOOK SOMETHING LIKE:

 - 9+ years of professional engineering experience, excluding internships, in backend, platform, or product engineering roles.

 - A track record of hands-on technical leadership, including setting architecture, breaking complex problems into clear implementation plans, and guiding engineers through delivery.

 - Deep backend engineering and systems design skills, with proficiency in at least one backend programming language and experience designing services, data models, and interfaces that remain reliable as usage grows.

 - End-to-end ownership of complex systems or product capabilities, from ambiguous requirements and technical design through implementation, launch, and production iteration.

 - Strong production engineering judgment: you can diagnose difficult failures, reason about performance and scalability, and improve reliability through testing, observability, and operational discipline.

 - Strong product judgment that connects technical decisions to user needs, with the ability to balance delivery speed, reliability, security, and long-term maintainability.

 - The ability to move between backend infrastructure and product experiences, contribute across the stack when needed, and quickly learn unfamiliar systems, tools, and domains.

 - Clear technical communication and effective collaboration across disciplines, including explaining trade-offs, creating alignment, and driving complex work forward while remaining hands-on.

 - Experience with AI agents, enterprise workflows, integrations, or agent development and evaluation is a plus, but not required.

title: Product Content Creator
descriptionPlain:
About the Team

The B2B Content team helps business audiences understand what AI makes possible and how to put it to work. We develop narrative, editorial, demo, and adoption programs that connect OpenAI’s products to concrete business value.

We partner closely with Product Marketing, Demand Generation, Customer Education, Sales, and other teams to create content that is useful on its own and supports the broader customer journey.

We value people who are eager to learn, have a bias for action, and look beyond the immediate deliverable. We build the tools, systems, and shared practices that help the whole team produce better work over time.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Product Content Creator to help create the next generation of AI-native marketing content. You’ll develop videos, interactive tutorials, live demos, written guides, and other experiences that help business audiences understand what AI makes possible and how it applies to their work.

This is a hands-on creative role spanning demand generation and product adoption. You’ll explore product capabilities, build and test workflows, and produce content for campaigns that introduce people to useful ideas and help them put those ideas into practice. You’ll maintain evergreen campaign content and develop new adoption campaigns, using practical workflows, research, and thought leadership as source material.

You’ll use Codex and other AI tools to prototype ideas and create experiences that would previously have required a larger production team. We’re looking for the fluency of a coding-assistant power user; an engineering background isn’t required. Strong judgment about the idea, the audience, and the finished experience matters as much as the ability to build it.

You’ll partner with Product Marketing on positioning and product accuracy, Demand Generation on campaign goals and distribution needs, and Demo Studio on demonstrations and production. You’ll own the content from concept through delivery, choosing the format that best serves the idea and the audience. This is an individual-contributor role for someone who enjoys making, explaining, experimenting, and shipping.

The role is hybrid and will be based in San Francisco, Monday through Wednesday. Thursday and Friday are work-from-home days, with occasional in-office attendance as needed for live webinars.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop creative concepts and produce content for Demand Generation campaigns, grounded in audience needs, product workflows, research, and expert perspectives.

 - Personally create videos, interactive tutorials, live demos, and written guides, carrying work from the initial idea through a finished asset.

 - Use Codex and other AI tools to build and test workflows, prototype interactive experiences, and improve how content is produced.

 - Develop and test original content formats, learn from audience response, and turn the strongest ideas into recurring series or reusable campaign experiences. Choose formats for what they help the audience understand or do.

 - Develop webinar content with the webinar strategist, including the storyline, presentation, demonstration, and useful follow-up resources.

 - Work with Product Marketing, subject-matter experts, and Demo Studio to make content accurate, substantive, and engaging.

 - Work with customer-facing teams to learn how people actually use the products, where they get stuck, and which workflows are worth demonstrating. Use those insights to develop relevant stories and adoption content.

 - Adapt strong ideas across formats and audiences while giving each asset a clear purpose within the campaign.

 - Deliver usable campaign assets to Demand Generation, with clear audience framing, supporting copy, and a proposed next action.

 - Use audience feedback and campaign results with DG to improve the content, and keep reusable workflows, examples, and source material current.

 - Maintain evergreen campaign content, updating workflows, demonstrations, and supporting resources as products and audience needs change.

 - Create adoption campaign content that helps people try relevant workflows, overcome common difficulties, and continue using them in their work.

 - Review campaign results and audience feedback with partners to understand both what attracts interest and what helps people successfully use the product.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a portfolio of substantive content you personally created across several formats, such as video, interactive tutorials, live demos, and written guides. Work projects, side projects, and experiments driven by your own curiosity are all relevant—we want to understand what you made and the decisions behind it.

 - Are a confident user of Codex or comparable coding assistants and can show how you used them to build, test, and improve something useful. An engineering background isn’t required.

 - Bring strong creative and editorial judgment: you can recognize an interesting idea, explain why a format works, and improve an experience beyond the first version.

 - Can learn a product deeply enough to demonstrate real workflows and explain them clearly to business audiences with different levels of technical fluency.

 - Write clearly, communicate well on video or in live demonstrations, and can turn complex material into something people want to spend time with.

 - Understand how content supports marketing campaigns and can work with Demand Generation on audience needs, campaign goals, and what the results suggest changing.

 - Take ownership from an ambiguous brief through delivery, balancing experimentation with the practical work required to ship.

 - May have developed these skills in product marketing, developer relations, product education, creative technology, or content marketing.

OpenAI's Legal team plays a crucial role in furthering OpenAI's mission by tackling innovative, fundamental legal issues in AI. We partner closely with Sales, Revenue Operations, Finance, Product, Enablement, Program Management, and external BPO partners to drive advertiser acquisition, activation, revenue growth, and retention.

You will design the governance, performance systems, capacity plans, quality programs, and accountability mechanisms that enable our BPO partners to deliver exceptional commercial outcomes. You will work across internal teams and external partner leadership to improve seller productivity, advertiser growth, forecasting accuracy, and operational quality.

This is a highly cross-functional individual contributor role that sits at the intersection of Ads Sales, SMB, Revenue Operations, Finance, Enablement, Product, Program Management, and external BPO leadership. You will help define how OpenAI operates with external partners and build the systems, processes, and accountability mechanisms that enable the business to scale.

This role is based in Sydney. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

title: Deployment Strategist
descriptionPlain:
Who we are

Picogrid is a leading venture-backed defense technology company founded to bridge the decades-long gap between modern technology and the critical demands of national security. Today, we're building the essential infrastructure to unify sensors, autonomy, and operators with our technology deployed in active operations around the world. Our mission is to deliver an operational advantage to secure the United States and its allies.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Deployment Strategist at Picogrid, you will deploy and operationalize our platform in complex, real-world environments. You will work directly with warfighters and government program stakeholders to understand mission needs, translate them into clear plans, and coordinate the people, technology, and decisions required to deliver operational outcomes.

This is not a traditional engineering role or a conventional customer-success position. It combines technical fluency, customer relationship ownership, program execution, and hands-on field operations. Your focus is making each assigned engagement successful: establishing the plan, coordinating internal and external teams, preparing field activity, resolving blockers, and closing the loop on outcomes.

You will work closely with experienced Deployment Strategists, Forward Deployed Engineers, Product, Engineering, Logistics, Capture, and other operational leaders. You will begin with a defined set of engagements and grow your scope as you demonstrate sound judgment and consistent execution. The role requires travel up to 50%, including to military installations, exercises, demonstrations, and customer sites.

This is a role for someone who wants meaningful ownership early in their career, learns quickly across technical domains, and wants to see their work produce real outcomes in the field.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Drive day-to-day execution of assigned customer engagements, contracts, pilots, exercises, and deployments from kickoff through delivery and follow-through

 - Translate customer objectives and ambiguous mission needs into clear scopes, timelines, responsibilities, technical requirements, and decision points

 - Serve as a primary point of coordination for assigned customers, building trust through proactive communication, responsiveness, and consistent delivery

 - Coordinate across Engineering, Product, Logistics, Capture, external partners, and customer teams to keep integrated efforts aligned and moving

 - Capture customer and product insights to drive growth identifying appropriate opportunities to expand applications of Picogrid technologies

 - Plan and support field activities, including site coordination, readiness reviews, equipment and personnel requirements, execution, and after-action follow-up

 - Maintain accurate engagement records and provide timely inputs for contract, invoicing, deliverable, and program reporting

 - Identify operational, technical, or schedule risks early; develop practical mitigation plans; and escalate issues with the context needed for decisions

 - Gather feedback from operators and program stakeholders and translate it into actionable input for product improvements, deployment practices, and future engagement planning

 - Document decisions, customer context, and repeatable processes so engagements can scale and transition without losing mission knowledge

WHO YOU ARE

 - You turn ambiguity into action by identifying what is known, asking the right questions, and building an executable plan

 - You take ownership within your scope, follow through on commitments, and know when a risk or decision should be escalated

 - You develop working knowledge of technical systems quickly and can explain requirements and tradeoffs across engineers, operators, government stakeholders, and external partners

 - You earn trust through preparation, sound judgment, discretion, and reliable execution

 - You communicate clearly and concisely, surface risks early, and keep the right people informed without creating unnecessary process

 - You are collaborative, low-ego, and comfortable working alongside customers and technical teams in the field

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

 - 2+ years of experience in deployments, military operations, technical program or project execution, customer-facing operations, consulting, or a related role

 - Demonstrated experience owning a customer-facing technical or operational workstream from planning through delivery

 - Experience coordinating complex work across customers, technical teams, and other stakeholders

 - Technical fluency and the ability to understand integrated hardware and software systems well enough to support planning, troubleshooting, and customer communication

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief technical, operational, and leadership audiences

 - Willingness and ability to travel up to 50%, sometimes on short notice, to military installations, exercises, and customer sites

 - Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience working with the U.S. military, Department of Defense, or other national-security organizations

 - An active U.S. Government security clearance

 - Experience supporting field deployments, military exercises, pilots, demonstrations, or test events

 - Familiarity with command and control, autonomy, robotics, sensors, communications, or other integrated mission systems

 - Experience working at a startup, high-growth company, or another environment where processes are still being built

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Picogrid’s growth depends on more than building strong technology. We must translate that technology into reliable outcomes for customers operating in demanding environments. As our portfolio expands, every customer engagement needs a clear owner who can maintain mission context, coordinate execution, and earn the trust of the operators involved.

This role ensures assigned engagements have someone driving action, resolving gaps, and closing the loop between the customer and Picogrid. By staying close to operators and technical teams, Deployment Strategists turn field feedback into better deployments, better product decisions, and repeatable practices that allow Picogrid to scale without losing operational intimacy.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Base salary range: $100,000–$160,000 per year. Base salary is just one part of your total compensation package at Picogrid.

 - Significant stock options with a high potential upside as an early-stage company

 - 401(k) with employer matching

 - Health coverage for you and your family (medical, dental, and vision insurance)

 - Relocation assistance provided (if applicable)

 - Unlimited PTO (two-week minimum) and 13 paid holidays per year

 - Paid parental leave for both parents

 - Lunch provided when working in-office and a fully stocked kitchenette

 - Free EV charging at the HQ

 - Unique office in El Segundo, CA stocked with quality coffee, snacks, and craft beer

EXPORT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.
