title: Behavior Management Engineering Lead
descriptionPlain:
Who we are

Picogrid is a leading venture-backed defense technology company founded to bridge the decades-long gap between modern technology and the critical demands of national security. Today, we're building the essential infrastructure to unify sensors, autonomy, and operators with our technology deployed in active operations around the world. Our mission is to deliver an operational advantage to secure the United States and its allies.

ABOUT THE ROLE

At 0200, three cameras swing toward the fence line at once. A rule the day shift wrote is doing it. The night operator needs to see which rule fired and stop it in one click. That is the software you will build: rules that slew a camera onto a radar track, hand a threat to the right response system the moment an operator confirms it, or release a camera when its track goes stale. Operators write these rules, watch them run, and step in when they misbehave. Your job is to make that simple and safe.

You will own the backend orchestration and operator experience together: triggers, conditions, task sequences, permissions, and a record of what actually happened. Decide when stale information should release a camera, how two rules share a device, and which actions need human approval. Your code connects decisions in the interface to commands at the edge. Picogrid runs in major Army and joint exercises back to back, four of them in under two months, and every new integration adds behavior that operators must be able to supervise and stop.

You will own a vertical or customer segment of behavior management. This is a hands-on technical lead role with product responsibility, from sitting with operators and choosing the first workflows to writing code and testing it with hardware. As the area grows, you will choose the skills the team needs and recruit engineers to own behavior execution and operator workflows. Show us a system you put in users' hands, what confused them, and what you changed. Work from a company, a lab, or an independent project can demonstrate that judgment.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Build the rule and task lifecycle, from an operator's initial configuration through activation, execution, cancellation, and review.

 - Define arbitration between competing behaviors, including device ownership, priority, timeouts, and what happens when an operator takes manual control.

 - Ship interfaces that show why a behavior started, which commands succeeded, what is waiting for approval, and how to suspend automation.

 - Establish safety interlocks and approval boundaries with operators and integration engineers, then enforce them in the execution path.

 - Design edge execution for missing telemetry, delayed acknowledgments, interrupted connections, and restarts without silently repeating physical actions.

 - Own simulation, hardware tests, and event replay that let engineers reproduce a failed sequence and operators rehearse a proposed rule before enabling it.

 - Set the technical roadmap and help hire and mentor engineers as recurring workflows become shared product capabilities.

YOUR FIRST YEAR

 - Start by watching operators create, hand off, and stop automated rules, then ship a rule-authoring and supervision improvement within your first 30 days.

 - Test competing rules against real cameras, including lost telemetry and manual takeover, then have an operator trace each action to its cause and stop the workflow.

 - Deliver a reusable multi-device workflow with explicit approval points, visible execution state, and a tested stop path.

 - Recruit the first additional engineers and give each a behavior execution or operator workflow capability to ship, with clear ownership and acceptance criteria.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Evidence of taking a software system from uncertain requirements through deployment, direct user feedback, and continued operation.

 - Ability to implement backend services and operator-facing workflows, with substantial depth in at least one and willingness to own both.

 - Experience reasoning about asynchronous events, state machines, concurrency, cancellation, and partial failure in production software.

 - Evidence of turning complex system behavior into an interface users can understand and control.

 - Ability to explain architectural tradeoffs, review code, and guide other engineers while remaining a hands-on contributor.

 - U.S. citizenship and ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with robotics, industrial automation, fleet management, or other software that commands physical equipment.

 - Experience with workflow engines, behavior trees, planning systems, or declarative rule languages.

 - Experience building with Go, Python, TypeScript, or React and deploying services on Linux edge computers.

 - Experience with safety analysis, authorization models, audit trails, or human approval workflows.

 - Experience running hardware-in-the-loop tests and observing users during field exercises.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Base salary range: $200,000 - $280,000 per year. Base salary is just one part of your total compensation package at Picogrid.

 - Significant stock options with a high potential upside as an early-stage company

 - 401(k) with employer matching

 - Health coverage for you and your family (medical, dental, and vision insurance)

 - Relocation assistance provided (if applicable)

 - Unlimited PTO (two-week minimum) and 13 paid holidays per year

 - Paid parental leave for both parents

 - Lunch provided when working in-office and a fully stocked kitchenette

 - Free EV charging at the HQ

descriptionPlain:
Who we are

Picogrid is a leading venture-backed defense technology company founded to bridge the decades-long gap between modern technology and the critical demands of national security. Today, we're building the essential infrastructure to unify sensors, autonomy, and operators with our technology deployed in active operations around the world. Our mission is to deliver an operational advantage to secure the United States and its allies.

ABOUT THE ROLE

A small boat comes toward a pier on base at 0300 with its lights off. A radar tracks it. The camera is on a separate console, and the operator has to connect the track to the video, assess the threat, and coordinate a response before the boat reaches the pier. You will build the base-defense software that lets the operator seamlessly coordinate sensors and unmanned systems using best-in-class products, even when they come from different vendors, don’t speak the same protocols, and weren’t designed to work together. You will develop cutting edge mission capabilities, used by warfighters in real-world environments.

Picogrid is deployed at U.S. bases, partnering with best-in-class systems to enable perimeter detection at all hours, from all directions. Your work will turn a base-defense problem into a capability that operators can learn and field teams can deploy repeatedly. The scope could center on waterside security, wildlife hazards around installations and airfields, counter-UAS, or point defense. Each calls for different sensing and response procedures. You own the path from operator conversations through design, code, field testing, and sustained use, building on Legion, Orion, and Expeditionary C2 Nodes across device integrations, backend services, and the operator interface.

You will own a vertical or customer segment within base defense. As the base-defense team grows, you will select engineers, set their responsibilities, and stay close to the code. Expect to defend a design decision, test it against real hardware, and watch an operator use it. We want to hear about a system you put in users' hands, what failed in use, and what you changed. You do not need a previous lead title to have done that work.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Define a focused capability roadmap with operators: which hazards or threats to surface, what evidence they need, and which response steps belong in software.

 - Build integrations for radars, cameras, and other sensors, carrying timestamps, location, identity, and device health through to the operator's view.

 - Build the base-defense operator workflow in Orion, our command and control application: inspect a track, cue a camera, acknowledge an alert, and hand the incident to the next operator with its observations and actions intact.

 - Design edge and cloud behavior so operators can distinguish fresh observations from stale data and see what remains available when connectivity fails.

 - Establish repeatable tests using recorded sensor data and real hardware, including nuisance detections, interrupted video, sensor restarts, and failed commands.

 - Lead field releases with deployment engineers, resolve failures across application and device boundaries, and turn site-specific lessons into reusable product changes.

 - Set engineering standards for your capability and help recruit and mentor the engineers who will share its ownership.

YOUR FIRST YEAR

 - By day 30, choose the first base-defense workflow with operators, watch how they handle it today, and ship an improvement that carries a sensor observation through to an operator action.

 - At your first field test, demonstrate the workflow with real sensors and document performance, failure cases, and operator feedback against agreed acceptance criteria.

 - Deliver a repeatable release and configuration process that lets a deployment engineer bring the capability to another site without a custom code branch.

 - Establish the next capability milestones and a hiring plan, then help select and onboard the first additional engineer as the scope grows.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Evidence that you have owned a substantial software system from an unclear requirement through deployment, user feedback, and maintenance.

 - Ability to write production code in Go, Python, TypeScript, or a comparable language and contribute across backend services and operator-facing applications.

 - Experience integrating hardware or external systems and debugging data or command failures across APIs, networks, and application state.

 - Sound judgment about asynchronous events, geospatial data, unreliable connections, and how to expose uncertainty to users.

 - Ability to explain technical tradeoffs, make scope decisions with users, and raise the quality of other engineers' work through review and mentoring.- Strong intuition about user journeys, and experience owning UI/UX for user-facing products.

 - Willingness to work with physical systems and travel for operator visits and field tests.

 - U.S. citizenship and ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with perimeter security, maritime sensing, wildlife monitoring, or point-defense systems.

 - Experience building live maps, video interfaces, alert workflows, or camera-control applications in React and TypeScript, with map libraries such as deck.gl http://deck.gl, Mapbox, MapLibre or Cesium.

 - Experience deploying and diagnosing Linux applications on field compute hardware with limited bandwidth or intermittent backhaul.

 - Experience with IoT and resource-optimized messaging protocols such as MQTT.

 - Familiarity with radar tracks, coordinate systems, sensor timing, and measuring detection or tracking performance.

 - Experience delivering integrations with TAK, Maven, Lattice, or other command-and-control systems.

title: Battlefield Management Mesh Engineering Lead
descriptionPlain:
Who we are

Picogrid is a leading venture-backed defense technology company founded to bridge the decades-long gap between modern technology and the critical demands of national security. Today, we're building the essential infrastructure to unify sensors, autonomy, and operators with our technology deployed in active operations around the world. Our mission is to deliver an operational advantage to secure the United States and its allies.

ABOUT THE ROLE

A forward site's satellite link drops for six hours. The tactical operations center (TOC) still needs to know what that site sees. You will build the software that decides what each node shares, which available path carries it, and how operators can tell when the map has fallen behind. When the link returns, the sites need to reconcile their pictures without reviving expired tracks.

Picogrid meshes feed the command and control systems above them. Legion connects the tactical edge to half a dozen C2 platforms in live operations and many more in exercises. You will own the distributed software that connects our Expeditionary C2 Nodes (ECNs) to one another and to Legion. That means peer discovery, secure connectivity, track distribution, and multi-site aggregation. The hard decisions are yours: which updates take priority on a constrained link, when a track is too old to use, and how nodes recover after losing contact.

You will own a vertical or customer segment of battlefield management mesh. Expect to write software, trace packets on field hardware, and work beside field engineers until another crew can set up the network without you. As the team grows, you will select engineers and give them clear ownership of transport, distributed data, and tactical integrations. We want to hear about a networked system you shipped, what broke in use, and what you changed. Apply even if that experience came early in your career.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Build peer-to-peer data distribution that keeps local sensor information available when Legion cloud connectivity disappears, with explicit rules for stale tracks and reconnection.

 - Design tiered meshes that let a TOC aggregate many sites without making every field node transmit the same data separately to every recipient.

 - Define forwarding contracts for track identity, origin, expiration, and loop prevention so relayed information does not multiply or outlive its source.

 - Engineer Legion Mesh, the secure overlay that connects nodes across satellite links, mesh radios, and wired networks, tracing latency and packet loss through direct and relayed paths.

 - Deliver TAK and Cursor on Target (CoT) integrations that preserve track identity, location, and freshness as information crosses C2 boundaries.

 - Set bandwidth budgets and test traffic prioritization under constrained links, balancing timely track updates against competing data flows.

 - Own release readiness with repeatable multi-node tests, useful network diagnostics, and field procedures that let another engineer isolate a broken data path.

YOUR FIRST YEAR

 - Your first 30 days: follow a track from sensor to peer, TOC, and cloud, measure where bandwidth and time go, and ship a change that reduces traffic or gets fresh information to operators sooner.

 - Complete a field test that interrupts uplinks, constrains radio bandwidth, and restarts nodes; document what operators can still see and how the picture recovers.

 - Deliver a repeatable multi-site setup that demonstrates aggregate visibility, bounded forwarding traffic, and correct track expiration in TAK.

 - Recruit the first mesh engineers and get each shipping an owned part of the network, with a multi-node test that shows how it behaves when a link fails.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Evidence that you took a networked software system from design through deployment and stayed responsible when it failed in use.

 - Ability to write and debug production software in Go, Rust, C++, or a comparable language, including concurrent services and network protocols.

 - Practical knowledge of IP routing, TCP/UDP, NAT, tunneling, and Linux networking, demonstrated through packet captures and root-cause diagnosis.

 - Experience reasoning about distributed state, message delivery, duplication, ordering, and failure recovery across unreliable connections.

 - Ability to turn an ambiguous operational need into a technical interface, explain the tradeoffs, and bring other engineers through implementation.

 - Willingness to work directly with hardware and operators during field testing and deployment.

 - U.S. citizenship and ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with tactical radios, satellite backhaul, mobile networks, or other bandwidth-constrained systems.

 - Experience building publish-subscribe messaging systems, including MQTT or comparable protocols.

 - Experience with MIL-STD data formats, geospatial data, or live sensor-track distribution.

 - Experience with cryptographic node identity, certificate lifecycles, and access controls for intermittently connected devices.

 - Experience hiring or mentoring engineers while retaining hands-on ownership of a shipped system.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Base salary range: $200,000 - $280,000 per year. Base salary is just one part of your total compensation package at Picogrid.

 - Significant stock options with a high potential upside as an early-stage company

 - 401(k) with employer matching

 - Health coverage for you and your family (medical, dental, and vision insurance)

 - Relocation assistance provided (if applicable)

 - Unlimited PTO (two-week minimum) and 13 paid holidays per year

 - Paid parental leave for both parents

 - Lunch provided when working in-office and a fully stocked kitchenette

 - Free EV charging at the HQ

 - Unique office in El Segundo, CA stocked with quality coffee, snacks, and craft beer

title: Bolt-On Autonomy Engineering Lead
descriptionPlain:
Who we are

Picogrid is a leading venture-backed defense technology company founded to bridge the decades-long gap between modern technology and the critical demands of national security. Today, we're building the essential infrastructure to unify sensors, autonomy, and operators with our technology deployed in active operations around the world. Our mission is to deliver an operational advantage to secure the United States and its allies.

ABOUT THE ROLE

A vehicle drives into a valley and loses GPS. It still has to know where it is. The computer bolted onto it must combine its inertial navigation system (INS) with visual-inertial odometry (VIO) to keep its position, track uncertainty and tell the operator who assigned the mission when it can no longer proceed safely. You will make navigation, vehicle control and operator intent work together under those conditions.

You will lead the software that adds autonomy to existing platforms through onboard compute and connected sensors. Your scope spans sensor discovery, navigation, vehicle control and mission assembly across ground vehicles, airframes, turrets and interceptors. It extends to full mission orchestration: automatic takeoff, meshing with other airframes in flight, and terminal flight with target acquisition on intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. That means deciding which interfaces can serve several platforms and which limits belong to a specific installation. You own the path from simulation to a bench with real hardware to an operator-supervised field test, including degraded navigation and communications. This work is funded: the Air Force awarded Picogrid a $3.2M program for unmanned systems integration.

You will own a vertical or customer segment of bolt-on autonomy. As this work grows, you will recruit engineers for navigation, platform integrations and mission execution, and decide how they share responsibility for a vehicle in the field. Expect to write software, set acceptance criteria and work directly with hardware engineers, platform partners and operators. We want to hear about hardware you put into use, what failed and how you corrected it. Apply even if your career has been short and you have already done that work.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Build capability discovery that identifies connected sensors and vehicles, rejects ambiguous membership, and tells the operator which mission functions are available.

 - Define navigation interfaces for an inertial navigation system (INS), including coordinate frames, installation geometry, timestamps, uncertainty and loss of a trustworthy position or heading.

 - Develop vehicle and turret control integrations with explicit command authority, operator takeover, cancellation and safe responses to lost communications.

 - Assemble and orchestrate full missions from navigation, sensing and control capabilities through Legion, from automatic takeoff to terminal flight, keeping platform-specific limits visible to planning software and operators.

 - Create simulation, hardware-in-the-loop tests and field procedures that exercise stale telemetry, sensor loss and GNSS-degraded operation before expanding the operating envelope.

YOUR FIRST YEAR

 - Lead an operator-supervised field test of an integrated vehicle and sensor package, with measured navigation quality, command latency and takeover behavior.

 - Bring a second platform or sensor configuration onto the shared interfaces and use the differences to remove assumptions tied to the first installation.

 - Recruit the first additional autonomy engineers, give each a defined subsystem to own, and establish how changes pass from simulation through hardware tests to field release.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - You have shipped software that controls or coordinates physical hardware and can explain your decisions, failures and test evidence.

 - You can build and debug production software on Linux in Go, Python, C++ or a comparable language, across application and device boundaries.

 - You understand coordinate transforms, timing and navigation uncertainty well enough to diagnose a plausible-looking but incorrect vehicle pose.

 - You have integrated third-party hardware or software from incomplete documentation and verified its actual behavior.

 - Experience building simulation, recorded-data replay or hardware-in-the-loop infrastructure that caught problems before a field test.

 - Experience conducting field trials with operators or growing a small engineering team while remaining a hands-on contributor.

title: Air Defense Engineering Lead
descriptionPlain:
Who we are

Picogrid is a leading venture-backed defense technology company founded to bridge the decades-long gap between modern technology and the critical demands of national security. Today, we're building the essential infrastructure to unify sensors, autonomy, and operators with our technology deployed in active operations around the world. Our mission is to deliver an operational advantage to secure the United States and its allies.

ABOUT THE ROLE

A radar sees a drone. The operator needs to understand the track, select an available interceptor, and share the air picture with the tactical operations center (TOC). Those steps cross equipment from different manufacturers, different coordinate systems, and networks that can drop out. You will own the software that makes that sequence work as a complete air defense capability.

Picogrid is deployed in counter-drone operations for the U.S. Army, where it recently connected 20 unique defense systems from different vendors into one picture, and its expeditionary air defense network integrates Ukraine-proven Shahed interceptors. Our systems power air defense applications in countries around the world. Your scope connects radar and interceptor integrations, an operator C2 application on an Expeditionary C2 Node (ECN), and track handoff to higher-echelon command systems through Legion. Expect to write code, settle interface questions with partners, and test with operators. A week can include tracing an old track through a packet capture, changing a map interaction, and testing the resulting software on field hardware.

You will own a vertical or customer segment within air defense. As the air defense team grows, you will recruit engineers and divide ownership across integrations, operator workflows, and C2 interoperability. The complete mission workflow remains your responsibility. We want to hear about a project where you resolved unclear requirements, shipped the software, and stayed responsible when users put it to work. Apply if you have done that, even early in your career or without a previous lead title.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Build radar and interceptor integrations that preserve track identity, timestamps, coordinates, device status, and command acknowledgments across vendor interfaces.

 - Define the operator workflow from track selection through interceptor tasking, including explicit authorization, visible command state, and clear handling of rejected or interrupted actions.

 - Specify track handoff contracts with higher-echelon C2 partners, then demonstrate that the receiving system interprets the data correctly.

 - At your first field test, demonstrate the radar-to-operator-to-interceptor workflow and higher-echelon track handoff. Record track freshness, command acknowledgments, and any gaps between the tested configuration and the intended deployment.

 - Turn the tested configuration into a repeatable release, including regression scenarios for stale tracks, device restarts, and lost connectivity.

 - Recruit and onboard the first air defense engineers. Give each engineer an interface or workflow to own and a concrete delivery target for the next field event.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Evidence that you owned a substantial software project from uncertain requirements through deployment and support, whether at work, in research, or on an independent team.

 - Ability to write and review production software in Go, Python, TypeScript, C++, or a comparable language, and follow a failure across application and network boundaries.

 - Experience integrating external hardware or software through documented and undocumented interfaces, including diagnosing mismatches with logs, packet captures, or test equipment.

 - Ability to explain technical tradeoffs to users and partners, define testable acceptance criteria, and direct a small engineering effort while contributing code.

ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re seeking someone to lead the future of fraud machine learning at Ramp. In this role, you will help build core machine learning models, design data architectures, and set strategic roadmaps to help Ramp mitigate fraud-related threats while minimizing the friction experience by legitimate users. You will partner closely with product and engineering counterparts across model design, implementation, execution, and analysis.

title: Cost Accounting Manager
descriptionPlain:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

Job Overview

We are seeking a Cost Accounting Manager to join our Accounting team supporting Saronic’s rapid growth. This role owns the core cost accounting processes, including standard costing, product costing, inventory valuation, and the cost accounting components of the month-end close. You will become an expert in our products, their manufacturing processes, and their costs, and ensure accurate, auditable financial reporting of inventory and cost of goods sold.

You will work closely with Manufacturing Finance, Supply Chain Finance, Production, Manufacturing Engineering, and Inventory Control to ensure information flows cleanly between our systems and that inventory transactions are recorded and valued correctly. You will define the standards of excellence for cost accounting at Saronic and build processes that scale with the business.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys owning a function end to end, working side by side with production teams, and building resilient, controlled processes in a fast-moving, high-growth manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities

 - Own the standard costing process. Maintain cost accounting standards and standard costs for finished goods and production components in the ERP, including cost roll-ups that incorporate raw material standards from Supply Chain Finance and overhead rates from Manufacturing Finance.

 - Own inventory valuation. Own the inventory costing process and the related financial reporting impacts, including capitalization, absorption, and valuation in accordance with GAAP.

 - Own the cost accounting close. Own month-end close activities for inventory and cost accounting, including reconciliations, journal entries, reserves, and support schedules, and ensure accurate and timely reporting.

 - Analyze variances. Lead analysis of purchase price, usage, labor, overhead, and yield variances and other anomalies, and prepare clear explanations of discrepancies for senior management.

 - Ensure ERP integrity. Ensure the validity and accuracy of cost data and inventory records across PMS, MES, and ERP systems through analysis, internal audit, and coordination with Inventory Control, Production, and Manufacturing Engineering.

 - Partner with Manufacturing Finance and Supply Chain Finance. Coordinate on overhead pools and rates, raw material standard costs, and the financial impact of production and sourcing decisions.

 - Partner with production and operations. Work with Production, Manufacturing Engineering, and Supply Chain teams to understand variances, resolve root causes, and improve how inventory transactions flow through the systems.

 - Define standards and controls. Define the standards of excellence for cost accounting, and design and implement controls and practices that prevent systemic issues and support audit readiness.

 - Drive process improvement and automation. Identify and execute improvements across production, cost accounting, and supply chain processes, and streamline and automate complex processes to improve accuracy and efficiency.

 - Support decision-making. Prepare financial analysis of manufacturing costs, inventory, and expense information to support leadership decisions.

 - Support audits and technical accounting. Support internal and external audits and apply sound technical accounting judgment to inventory and cost accounting matters.

 - Anticipate risks. Identify risks to cost accuracy and inventory valuation early, mobilize resources to address them, and make decisive calls in ambiguous situations.

Required Qualifications

 - 7-9 years of accounting experience, including significant cost accounting experience in a manufacturing environment

 - Hands-on experience with standard costing, including cost roll-ups, variance analysis, and inventory valuation

 - Strong grasp of GAAP and cost accounting principles for inventory and cost of goods sold, and of inventory management practices

 - Experience owning month-end close activities for inventory and cost accounting

title: Shipyard Technical Manager
descriptionPlain:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

As the Shipyard Technical Manager at Saronic-Franklin, you will lead the technical execution and operational integration of Production and Engineering activities across the shipyard. This role is responsible for ensuring vessel construction activities are technically sound, production-ready, efficiently executed, and aligned with quality, schedule, and safety objectives.

The Shipyard Technical Manager will oversee the production engineering team, which supports scheduling, planning, production flow analysis and improvement, industrial engineering activities, and provides expertise across all labor trades in the shipyard. The Shipyard Technical Manager will also oversee the Manufacturing Engineering team, which supports workstation tooling, processes, and improvements, operates the machine shop, and recommends product design improvements. Finally, the Shipyard Technical Manager will work directly with the Design Engineering and Build Engineering leadership to ensure cross-functional agreement on product design improvements. This position plays a critical role in enabling scalable and repeatable vessel construction operations within a fast-paced maritime manufacturing environment.

KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY

1. Team Leadership: Manage, train, and motivate a team of production and manufacturing engineering personnel, including hiring, performance evaluations, and professional development.

2. Engineering Oversight: Ensure production and manufacturing engineering deliverables support efficient vessel construction, including work packages, installation planning, technical issue resolution, and production readiness.

3. Production and Manufacturing Engineering Management: Identify and implement continuous improvement initiatives related to production flow, scheduling, planning, build sequencing, and technical operations performance. Develop and optimize manufacturing processes, tooling strategies, workflow layouts, and resource utilization to improve workstation efficiency, reduce waste, and support scalable shipyard operations.

4. Build Engineering Coordination: Coordinate with build engineering leadership to ensure effective execution of activities related to structural assembly, vessel systems integration, outfitting coordination, and product design improvements to ensure technical alignment across departments.

5. Quality Assurance: Ensure engineering and manufacturing activities comply with company standards, shipyard procedures, regulatory requirements, and applicable maritime industry specifications.

6. 8. Safety Compliance: Work with the EHS team to enforce workplace safety protocols and ensure engineering-driven production activities are executed in accordance with Saronic EHS guidelines and company policies.

7. Reporting and Operational Metrics: Monitor and report key performance indicators (KPIs) related to production efficiency, engineering throughput, build execution, schedule performance, labor utilization, downtime for repair (DFR), and technical issue resolution.

Shipyard Technical Managers at Saronic-Franklin are expected to have the knowledge, skill, and ability to accomplish the below:

TECHNICAL KNOWLEDGE

1. Strong understanding of shipyard production operations, vessel construction sequencing, manufacturing processes, and marine production systems.

2. Ability to lead cross-functional engineering and production teams in a fast-paced shipbuilding environment.

3. Experience interpreting engineering drawings, production work packages, technical specifications, and vessel integration requirements.

4. Ability to analyze and make key operational decisions related to production workflows, staffing, manufacturing methods, tooling, and engineering priorities.

5. Ability to communicate effectively with executive leadership, engineering teams, production personnel, suppliers, and shipyard stakeholders.

6. Strong technical aptitude, organizational skills, and attention to detail.

7. Maintain proper administrative records, technical documentation, and operational reporting.

JOB PROFICIENCY

1. Ensure Production Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering teams are accomplishing tasks, roles, and responsibilities as outlined in applicable job descriptions and operational objectives.

2. Provide independent judgement to leadership regarding team performance, staffing needs, organizational structure, and operational improvements using established policies, procedures, and practices.

3. Resolve and document technical production issues impacting vessel construction, manufacturing operations, quality, or schedule performance.

4. Manage overall technical resource utilization to meet or exceed production and operational efficiency goals.

5. Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on manufacturing efficiency, production scalability, technical execution, and operational excellence.

6. Provide periodic operational documentation, technical status updates, engineering issue reporting, and shift turnover communication for compliance and continuous improvement purposes.

7. Collaborate with product design team, project management team, and build engineering team to ensure product design is in line with scaled production goals. This includes participating in conflict resolution re: design vs production issues

1. Facilitating as-built updates to drawings

2. Deriving, tracking, and implementing lessons learned in design-for-production

3. Facilitating design-for-production improvements

CULTURE AND COLLABORATION

1. Follow all shipyard safety policies, including proper use of PPE, fire prevention, and confined space protocols.

2. Assist in the training and development of all engineers and engineering management on site.

3. Collaborate and communicate effectively with all shipyard departments to ensure seamless vessel production integration.

4. Work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced maritime manufacturing environment.

5. Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work area.

6. Maintain a positive attitude toward customers and represent Saronic professionally.

title: Mechanic (Deployable)
descriptionPlain:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

JOB SUMMARY

Saronic is seeking a Mechanic IV to serve as the senior hands-on technician for our deployable maintenance footprint, supporting our autonomous platforms, including the 12 ft UUV, the 24 ft Corsair, and the 52 ft Mirage, at test sites, depots, and forward operating locations. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Deployable Operations within the Sustainment organization, you will diagnose, repair, and sustain diesel, mechanical, electrical, and integrated vehicle systems in the field and set the technical and quality standard the rest of the team works to.

This is the most senior wrench on the deck plate. Managers set priorities and own the schedule; junior technicians execute the routine work. You are the technical reference in between — the person who takes the hard diagnosis, decides the repair approach, verifies the quality of everyone else's work, and keeps operations moving when the answer is not in the manual. The ideal candidate has deep marine diesel experience, is credible across mechanical, electrical, and networked systems, and is comfortable working independently in remote, fast-moving environments with incomplete information.

Scope of the role

· Senior-level diagnosis, repair, and preventive maintenance across all supported platforms, CONUS and OCONUS

· Technical reference and quality standard for technicians at the assigned site or deployment

· Overhaul and rebuild support for diesel propulsion and associated systems

· Development and refinement of maintenance procedures, checklists, and troubleshooting guides based on field experience

· Mentorship, training, and quality verification for junior and mid-level technicians

· Field technical representation to engineers, operators, customers, and other stakeholders during operations and testing

How you support the mission

· Diagnose, repair, and troubleshoot diesel, mechanical, electrical, communications, networking, perception, sensor, power, and other integrated vehicle systems and subsystems.

· Perform inspections, preventive maintenance, repairs, component replacement, and system validation to return platforms to fully mission capable status.

· Execute complex diesel engine diagnostics, maintenance, and repair with high precision, and support overhaul and rebuild activities.

· Provide on-site technical leadership during field operations, testing, and customer events, coordinating effectively with technicians, engineers, operators, and customers.

· Clearly communicate equipment status, technical issues, risks, and recommended corrective actions to supervisors and stakeholders.

· Maintain accurate technical documentation, including maintenance records, troubleshooting notes, system configurations, test results, parts usage, and equipment deficiencies.

· Identify systemic quality issues and recurring failures, and recommend corrective actions to supervisors and the maintenance program.

· Proactively flag risks, parts shortfalls, or resource constraints before they impact operations or schedules.

· Travel approximately 80% of the time, including domestic and international assignments, to support field operations, testing, maintenance, and customer requirements.

How you support the team

· Set the quality standard on the shop floor and in field operations, and hold peers to that standard.

· Mentor and train personnel on equipment operation, troubleshooting, maintenance, and field procedures, and support quality verification for less experienced technicians.

· Develop and refine maintenance procedures, checklists, troubleshooting guides, and lessons learned so the team's knowledge outlives any single deployment.

· Serve as a key technical resource for cross-functional teams and field deployments, translating field realities into clear recommendations for engineering and leadership.

· Make informed decisions about complex maintenance workflows and repair approaches within your area, and communicate trade-offs to supervisors on challenging operational issues.

· Drive productivity within your area and take initiative to keep operations moving when issues arise.

· Support coverage of adjacent roles and help maintain operational continuity during staffing or scheduling gaps.

· Take full accountability for the quality, safety, and output of your assigned area or work scope, balancing thoroughness with urgency.

ROLE REQUIREMENTS

· 5+ years of hands-on diesel mechanical experience in marine, automotive, aerospace, heavy industrial, or a related technical field.

· Proven experience troubleshooting and maintaining complex mechanical, electrical, and integrated systems.

· Working knowledge of electrical systems, communications equipment, networking, sensors, and perception systems.

· Ability to work independently and effectively within cross-functional engineering and operations teams.

· Willingness and ability to travel approximately 80%, including extended domestic and international assignments.

· Ability to work flexible schedules, including evenings, weekends, and extended days when operationally required.

· Able to certify as "fit for work" by demonstrating ability to swim and tread water, lift up to 50 lbs., and spend extended time periods on the water.

QUALIFICATIONS

title: Deputy Program Manager, Test Range
descriptionPlain:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

JOB OVERVIEW

The Test Range Coordinator is Saronic’s primary interface to U.S. Government test ranges for live-fire, missile, and target test events conducted aboard our autonomous surface vessels. You will own the end-to-end coordination of each range event — from initial scheduling and safety approvals, through launcher installation and checkout, vessel movement to the range, ordnance onload, and live test execution, to post-event launcher de-installation and demobilization. Acting as the connective tissue between Saronic engineering and operations, the Government customer, payload and effector providers, and the range authorities, you will make sure every stakeholder has the access, documentation, and information needed to execute a safe, on-schedule, and successful test.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Range scheduling & access

 - Serve as Saronic’s single point of contact to U.S. Government test ranges — including Cape Canaveral Space Force Station / Space Launch Delta 45 (Eastern Range), the Point Mugu Sea Range (NAWCWD, Naval Base Ventura County), and the Pacific Missile Range Facility (PMRF) — as well as other Major Range and Test Facility Base (MRTFB) sites as programs require.

 - Submit, track, and maintain range-use requests and Universal Documentation System (UDS) products (e.g., Program Introduction, Program Requirements, and Operations Requirements documents), and negotiate and lock test windows on range schedules.

 - Coordinate range instrumentation, tracking, optics, telemetry, and Time-Space-Position Information (TSPI) requirements, along with frequency/spectrum requests, with range personnel.

 - Manage schedule conflicts, slip planning, and re-baselining across multiple concurrent test campaigns.

Safety, ordnance & regulatory approvals

 - Develop and shepherd range safety packages, hazard analyses, mission rules, and launch commit criteria through range safety and flight safety boards.

 - Coordinate ordnance transportation, explosives safety siting, and Explosives Safety Quantity-Distance (ESQD) requirements in accordance with DoD and range explosives safety standards.

 - Coordinate ordnance/effector onload, staging, arming and de-arming, and disposition, including Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) and range safety support.

 - Support environmental and regulatory compliance, including Notices to Mariners and Airmen (NOTMAR/NOTAM) and marine-mammal and environmental monitoring requirements.

Test event planning & execution

 - Build and maintain the integrated schedule for each test event, spanning launcher hardware installation, checkout, vessel movement to the range, ordnance onload, execution, and de-installation.

 - Coordinate logistics for vessel transport to and from the range (over-the-road and/or marine transit), launch and recovery, and support and safety craft.

 - Lead Test Readiness Reviews (TRRs), rehearsals and dry runs, and go/no-go processes, and run day-of coordination among range control, the Saronic test team, and payload providers.

 - Manage post-test launcher de-installation, demobilization, range clearance, and event close-out, including data hand-off and lessons learned.

Stakeholder & information management

 - Act as the information hub across Saronic, the Government customer, and payload/effector providers, maintaining shared schedules, action-item logs, interface documentation, and status reporting.

 - Coordinate the flow of technical and programmatic information, including handling of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and classified material in accordance with program security requirements.

 - Facilitate interface control between Saronic vessel and launcher hardware and third-party effectors, missiles, and targets (e.g., aerial and surface target drones).

 - Support the agreements and funding mechanisms that enable range use

QUALIFICATIONS

title: Electrical Engineer, Maneuver Dominance
descriptionPlain:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

  A  BOUT THE TEAM

 The Maneuver Dominance team at Anduril develops operationally relevant, multi-asset autonomy. We are focused on new air vehicle development programs, and making large groups of autonomous systems work effectively together.

 Within the Maneuver Dominance team, we are growing an early-stage, undisclosed autonomous air vehicle (AAV) program at our Costa Mesa HQ. This team is chartered with re-inventing an existing platform through heavy modification and integration of advanced autonomy, mission systems, and payloads.

 On this team, you will be tackling novel challenges across airframe, structures, avionics, and software from day one. As part of this program, you'll work alongside a tight-knit group of mechanical, structural, electrical, and software engineers, together with Program Leads and the Chief Engineer, all embedded in a single team driving toward major milestones.

 You will work in a lean, high-ownership culture where the entire vehicle team sits side-by-side, iterating quickly and making decisions in real time. Given the early stage of the program, you will have influence over foundational architecture decisions and the opportunity to redefine an existing platform.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

 In this position, you will work closely with the program leadership and a wide spectrum of cross-departments as part of a team focused on solving hard problems and changing the industry forever. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 The Manufacturing Development Process (MDP) team defines the ‘What’, ‘When’, ‘Why’ and ‘How’ for Manufacturing, from new product development (NPD) and new product introduction (NPI) to manufacturing operations. MDP is a comprehensive framework that enables Manufacturing Engineering teams to pull production readiness to the left and produce effectively at scale - highlighting key activities, deliverables, and cross-functional touchpoints to identify and escalate manufacturing risks early enough to inform engineering decisions.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 Anduril’s Manufacturing Development Process team is seeking a Senior Project Manager, Manufacturing Development to expand MDP across multiple product lines varying in process, cost, and schedule complexity. This role includes introducing, tailoring, and managing the rollout of MDP to multiple Divisions and Business Lines, tracking implementation progress, product health, and manufacturing risks, and developing and deploying tailored templates and resources. As a liaison between the Manufacturing Engineering team and all of its cross-functional partners (Program Management, Design Engineering, Quality, Test, etc.), this role develops business cases for technical solutions to align all teams on the approach to production.

If you are looking for a unique opportunity that is 70% project management and 30% manufacturing expertise, then this role is for you. You will bridge the gap between technical project management and production program management to improve manufacturing readiness and reduce manufacturing risk, measuring success by adoption of MDP as the playbook for production success - not by product delivery or cost avoidance. The successful candidate will have a mix of both business and technical acumen, with a strong focus on the product lifecycle and concurrent engineering principles.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO

 Introduce the MDP framework to a diverse set of stakeholders and programs. Socialize the business process and accompanying resources with cross-functional teams, including Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Operations, Design Engineering, Supply Chain, Program Management, Configuration Management, Quality, and more.

Align manufacturing milestones with integrated program schedules, establish accountability for MDP execution, track progress, facilitate action item closure, personalize resources, and prioritize team activities and deliverables.

 Communicate the importance of MDP and how it contributes to production success to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, from individual contributors to executives. Develop and deploy tailored communication strategies to match stakeholder interests when articulating manufacturing readiness to cross-functional audiences.

Build strategic business cases that highlight and communicate manufacturing risk to executive audiences, critically thinking through options and varying impacts to production to enable informed decision-making.

 Create tactical resources to execute MDP beyond the business process and help define what good looks like. Balance standardization with flexibility to create structure without killing speed, fostering meaningful adoption.

 Build relationships and influence change. Collaborate closely with engineers, program managers, product developers, and technicians to deeply understand their pain points, needs, and workflows. Advocate for manufacturing while recognizing the broader environment in which all of Anduril is operating.

 8+ years of experience overall in relevant domains.

 Direct hardware development experience with strong business acumen.

 Business process creation, development, rollout, and adoption experience.

 Demonstrated ability to influence without authority and create lasting behavioral change.

 Understanding of the product lifecycle (design/development/production), as well as the purpose of each phase and its associated importance for manufacturing readiness.

 Bias toward action with ability to filter noise from signal in order to go after the right problems and solutions. Proven ability to execute operationally while also being able to step back and think strategically.

title: Principal Test & Evaluation Engineer - Networked Battlefield Systems
descriptionPlain:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 The Test & Evaluation Engineering Team at Anduril works across the entire spectrum of products and business lines, as well as all flight operations and test range management. Our team conducts full system-level development testing, new production acceptance testing, sub-component qualification testing, and much more. If it involves test, we lead the way.

  Overview

 Anduril is seeking a Principal Test Engineer to serve as the senior-most individual-contributor technical authority for test and evaluation across Connected Warfare's portfolio, including Eagle Eye, NGC2, Menace family of systems, and more. Where Staff and Lead Test Engineers own the test program for a specific system or campaign, this role is accountable for technical coherence across Connected Warfare's applications — supporting teams in shaping sound verification strategy, resolving the hardest cross-system integration and test problems, and raising the bar for how the division's test engineers plan, execute, and document their work.

This role sits above individual program ownership and below formal people management: you'll support Staff- and Lead-level test engineers across multiple concurrent campaigns by reviewing their test approaches and documentation for technical adequacy and coaching them through the hardest problems — not by owning or executing programs yourself. Your primary value is deep technical judgment brought to bear on other teams' work, not headcount or personal execution output. You'll be the person program leadership and engineering call when a test problem is genuinely hard, ambiguous, or spans more than one Connected Warfare system.

  What you’ll do

 Serve as the senior technical authority on test strategy across most of Connected Warfare's applications, providing technical oversight and support to the teams running the division's most complex, highest-risk, or multi-system test campaigns.

 Review and help program teams strengthen verification strategies — requirements-based, scenario-based, and operationally relevant — ensuring they scale across CW's software-enabled hardware and pure-software systems and properly incorporate customer-required standards and metrics.

 Act as connective tissue across Connected Warfare's individual test programs: identify where one program's test infrastructure, tooling, instrumentation, or lessons learned should be reused elsewhere in the division, and work with program teams to drive that reuse.

 Provide technical mentorship and escalation support to Staff and Lead Test Engineers running individual program test campaigns — reviewing test plans, execution approach, and reporting across developmental test, system integration (HIL/SIL), and operational assessment events (from lab integration through field validation), unblocking hard technical problems, and raising the technical rigor of test execution across the division. Step in hands-on only on the most technically demanding events where a program team needs direct help.

 Directly support T&E Test Process execution (e.g. Test Readiness Reviews (TRRs), technical milestone reviews, and customer acceptance events), representing CW's test posture with credibility to government and program stakeholders.

 Work with teams to confirm traceability from requirements through verification and validation results across CW programs, and help define and monitor test coverage, requirements verification, and defect closure metrics at a division level, not just program level.

 Support root-cause investigation on the hardest test findings and system anomalies, partnering directly with engineering to resolve issues that cross system or program boundaries.

 Represent Connected Warfare T&E in engineering design reviews (PDR/CDR) and technical exchanges with government customers and partner organizations as needed.

 Contribute to the technical hiring and onboarding of test engineers across Connected Warfare.

  Required Qualifications

 Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline (advanced degree preferred); equivalent relevant experience considered.

 10-14+ years of experience in system-level test and evaluation of integrated hardware/software systems, with 8+ years operating in a technical leadership or test lead capacity.

 Demonstrated technical depth across multiple Connected Warfare-relevant systems (e.g., tactical C2, sensor/mission autonomy platforms, networked datalinks) — not limited to a single program.

 Proven track record across the full test lifecycle — requirements development, HITL lab integration, developmental test, operational validation, and reporting — including experience reviewing and strengthening other teams' test approaches and documentation, not just running your own program.

 Strong experience with RF communications, tactical datalinks, and networked C2 systems in DoD operational environments.

 Demonstrated ability to mentor and technically direct other test engineers across concurrent programs without formal management authority — influencing through technical credibility.

 Deep familiarity with DoD and industry test processes, including MIL-STD test protocols and government verification practices.

 Skilled in assessing and reporting on test metrics at a program and cross-program level.

 Excellent communication and technical presentation skills, with demonstrated ability to brief senior internal leadership and government customers.

 Ability to travel periodically (up to 50%) for test execution at ranges and field sites.

 Active or immediately eligible for a U.S. Secret security clearance; eligibility for Top Secret/SCI strongly preferred.

 In this role, you will be subject to pre-employment and randomized substance screening, as required by the Company.

 Master's degree in Systems Engineering or a related technical field.

 Prior experience as Test Lead across multiple DoD programs (ACAT I/II or equivalent), including cross-program or cross-system responsibility.

 Knowledge of EMI/EMC testing, environmental testing (MIL-STD-810), and power/avionics standards (MIL-STD-1275, MIL-STD-1553/1760).

 Experience helping teams build or scale test automation frameworks, data analysis tooling, or test instrumentation used across multiple programs.

 Hands-on experience with CI/CD pipelines, software integration, and hardware-in-the-loop test environments.

 Experience conducting test activities in remote, austere, or tactical operational settings.

 Active Top Secret/SCI clearance.

 As a Supplier Quality Data Analytics Engineer, you will be embedded within the Supplier Quality Engineering organization and serve as the team's dedicated analytics partner.   ABOUT THE JOB

 Anduril's Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S) Manufacturing Engineering team is seeking a  Propulsion Manufacturing Engineer  to provide subject matter expertise on propulsion system manufacturing across our portfolio of autonomous aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering munitions. This position may be filled at either the Senior or Staff level depending on experience and qualifications. This role covers the full spectrum of propulsion technologies relevant to AD&S — air-breathing jet turbines, ramjets, and solid rocket motors — and is responsible for ensuring that propulsion hardware can be manufactured, assembled, tested, and integrated at production rate with the quality and reliability our programs demand.

 You will bring deep expertise in the manufacturing processes, materials, and quality requirements specific to propulsion systems. Your knowledge of how these systems are built — from turbine blade casting and combustion fabrication to solid propellant processing and nozzle manufacturing — is what makes you valuable. You are the person who knows what can go wrong in propulsion production and how to prevent it through design influence, process control, and supplier qualification.

 A critical part of this role is working directly with design engineers and program-level manufacturing engineers to evaluate propulsion designs for producibility, drive DFM improvements, and support the selection and qualification of propulsion suppliers and contract manufacturers. You will also support propulsion system test campaigns from a manufacturing engineering perspective, including integration, acceptance testing, and anomaly resolution. This is an inherently cross-functional role: you will work daily with supply chain, quality, operations, test engineering, and program teams.

  You must be able to work on-site Monday-Friday at our Costa Mesa, CA campus. Per Anduril's expansion plans, we anticipate this job will be based out of our new Long Beach, CA campus, beginning late 2027.

  WHAT YOU'LL DO

 Serve as a propulsion manufacturing engineering subject matter expert across AD&S programs, covering air-breathing turbines, ramjets, and solid rocket motors.

 Evaluate propulsion system designs for manufacturability, assembly, and cost — leading or supporting DFM/DFA reviews and driving design changes that improve producibility without compromising performance.

 Work directly with design engineers and program manufacturing engineers to translate propulsion manufacturing constraints into actionable design feedback.

 Assist in the selection and qualification of propulsion suppliers and contract manufacturers — assessing manufacturing capability, process maturity, quality systems, and cost competitiveness for propulsion-specific production.

 Conduct or participate in supplier manufacturing assessments for propulsion hardware, including facility reviews, process audits, special process qualification (casting, brazing, propellant processing, thermal spray), and production readiness evaluations.

 Develop and maintain manufacturing process requirements and standards for propulsion-specific processes including turbine component manufacturing, combustor and hot section fabrication, solid propellant mixing and casting, nozzle manufacturing, and propulsion system assembly and integration.

 Support propulsion system test campaigns from a manufacturing engineering perspective — including hardware preparation, instrumentation integration, acceptance test criteria, and post-test hardware disposition and anomaly investigation.

 Develop or contribute to should-cost models and cost-driver analyses for propulsion assemblies and components, identifying design and process changes that reduce unit cost at rate production.

 Partner with quality engineering to define or support inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and process controls specific to propulsion hardware — including non-destructive testing (NDT), dimensional inspection, and material certification requirements.

 Collaborate with supply chain to align propulsion manufacturing requirements with sourcing strategy, including long-lead material planning and sole/single source risk mitigation.

 Close the loop between production and test feedback, supplier performance data, and upstream design and process improvements.

 Build and maintain propulsion manufacturing knowledge within the ME organization — developing training materials, lessons-learned databases, and technical reference documents.

 Mentor and develop junior and mid-level engineers on propulsion manufacturing principles and supplier assessment methods (Staff level).

 Travel to production sites, propulsion suppliers, and test facilities (~20%, depending on business needs).

  REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field, OR equivalent full-time, relevant industry experience.

 12+ years of experience in propulsion manufacturing, propulsion engineering, or a closely related manufacturing discipline — with expertise in at least one propulsion type: air-breathing turbines, ramjets, or solid rocket motors.

 Strong technical knowledge of propulsion-specific manufacturing processes relevant to your area of expertise. Depending on specialty, this may include: investment casting and single-crystal blade production, combustor and hot section fabrication (welding, brazing, thermal barrier coatings), solid propellant formulation, mixing, casting and curing, nozzle and throat insert manufacturing (ablatives, refractory metals, carbon-carbon composites), ramjet combustor and inlet manufacturing, or propulsion system assembly, integration, and acceptance testing.

 Experience evaluating propulsion designs for manufacturability and translating findings into measurable improvements.

 Experience evaluating or qualifying propulsion suppliers — including special process qualification and production readiness assessments.

 Understanding of cost drivers in propulsion production, with experience building or contributing to should-cost models.

 Ability to read and critically evaluate propulsion system drawings, specifications, and test requirements for manufacturing implications.

 Working knowledge of relevant propulsion standards and specifications (MIL-STD, SAE AMS, JANNAF, AIAA standards as applicable).

 Proven ability to work cross-functionally across design engineering, manufacturing engineering, test engineering, supply chain, quality, and operations.

 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present technical findings to engineering leadership and drive alignment on design and process changes.

 Comfortable working across multiple programs simultaneously in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

 Hands-on experience with propulsion hardware — whether in a production, test, or integration environment. Technical credibility matters.

 Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

  PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 Master's degree or PhD in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, or a propulsion-related field

 Deep expertise spanning two or more propulsion types (turbines, ramjets, solid rocket motors).

 Experience in aerospace or defense propulsion production, particularly with qualified or flight-critical hardware.

 Familiarity with AS9100/AS9102 quality management systems and their application to propulsion hardware.

 Experience with energetic materials handling, storage, and safety requirements for solid rocket motor production.

 Knowledge of propulsion system qualification processes (ground test, environmental qualification, lot acceptance testing).

 Background in advanced materials and processes relevant to propulsion: superalloys, ceramics, ablatives, composite overwrap, thermal protection systems.

 Proficiency in CAD software (NX, CATIA, SolidWorks, or similar) sufficient to review designs independently.

 Experience with value engineering or formal cost reduction programs in a propulsion production environment.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 The Special Access Program Security team is responsible for ensuring the security of classified information for Anduril’s most sensitive programs and contracts. The team has individuals located across the country and works in a collaborative manner to ensure the security of Anduril and government information, and Anduril’s defense products.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 We are looking for a Contractor Special Access Program Security Officer (CSSO) to join our growing team in Costa Mesa, CA. This is a security position requiring a qualified security professional in support of special access program initiatives. As a CSSO, you will be responsible for the management, direction, administration and development of security programs and procedures for assigned programs that have contractually imposed security requirements beyond 32 CFR Part 117, National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM) Rule requirements to include DoDM 5205.07, Intelligence Community Directives (ICDs 703, 704, 505, and others as applicable), Security Classification Guides (SCGs), and Statements of Work. Key responsibilities include Personnel Security, Physical Security and program OPSEC/Program Protection planning. The CSSO will interface with government agencies regarding assigned program security matters and requirements and will be responsible for managing all security-related aspects of assigned programs in close collaboration with other Anduril CSSOs. This will require detailed knowledge of the government policies applicable to Special Access Program (SAP) security, as well as practical experience implementing this knowledge to a fast-paced, quickly scaling, and complex manufacturing environment. If you are someone who enjoys fast-paced and collaborative work, finding solutions to interesting challenges, and possess a “can do” attitude, then this role is for you!

 WHAT YOU’LL DO

 Knowledgeable in interpreting and implementing security guidance based on applicable ICDs, SEADs, 32 CFR Part 117. “NISPOM Rule,” DoDM 5205.07, and other policies, regulations, and processes as applicable.

 Perform all aspects of Customer Personnel Security Program requirements. This includes, guidance and assistance for validation of SAP access, access requirements, processing and eligibility and polygraph requests, nomination interviews, submission of investigative requests, and conducting SAP security briefings.

 Perform all aspects of Physical Security by providing day to day support for badging, access control and visitor control. Ensure all SCIF/SAP Facility documentation is current and up to date.

 Support program managers and personnel with classification guidance and other program related requirements, i.e., incoming and outgoing visit certifications, foreign travel reporting and proposal support.

 Ensure SAP material is properly controlled, transmitted, transported, packaged, safeguarded, and destroyed, as appropriate.

 Investigate security incidents and prepare required reports.

 Build and maintain a relationship with government security counterparts.

 Provide security awareness training as required by regulations and as requested by our customers.

 Work with IT and ISSO to ensure equipment being brought into the secure areas is authorized and approved.

 Assist and provide guidance on ICD 705 modifications/upgrades at company site(s).

 Collaborate and assist the ISSO / ISSM on management of information systems.

 Maintain personnel security records for special access programs to include the use of SIMS, DISS, JADE, and other systems as applicable.

 Conduct internal self-inspections and manage government Staff Assistance Visits and Customer Security Assessments on behalf of Anduril.

 Maintain classified material accountability records to include inventory lists, receipt and transmittal records and final disposition documentation.

 Maintain working knowledge in the preparation and maintenance of prime and subcontract DD254s.

 Develop and maintain the program's Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).

 In collaboration with the physical security team, maintain the program’s access control and alarm systems.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 Bachelor's degree in related discipline or equivalent education and work experience.

 At least four years’ experience working with special programs in a ACSSO or CSSO role.

 Ability to work independently and possess knowledge over the full range of security principles, including but not limited to identifying and evaluating program risks/vulnerability; implementing mitigating improvement; and disseminating security procedures/processes.

 Build and maintain relationships with government security counterparts.

  DoD Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility with current investigation and ability to maintain a DoD Top Secret clearance with Special Program accesses.

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 Willing to work extended hours in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment in a variety of program areas.

 Willingness to travel on company business (varies but probably less than 15%).
