descriptionPlain:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 About the role

 The Director, Manufacturing Analytics owns Manufacturing Analytics globally: every site, every product line, and every Manufacturing function across Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Operations, Supply Chain, Planning, and Warehousing / Material Management. The ambition is not better dashboards. It is that a division leader can tell whether they will hit rate before they miss it, and that when we argue about where to invest, the argument is settled by data rather than by whoever presents best.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 This is a player-coach role. You will lead the hardest analytical problems yourself, on the programs that matter most to the company, and build a team that can run several more in parallel. You will be judged on what you accomplish, not on how you operate: whether a program hit rate that would otherwise have slipped, whether a constraint got cleared because we saw it coming, whether a number leadership used to make a real decision came from this team.
We weigh approach over domain familiarity. The strongest analytics leaders we have are exceptional at how they attack a problem, even where they arrived without the functional background. Manufacturing depth is useful and listed below as preferred, but it does not substitute for analytical method, judgment about what matters, and the ability to drive a result through an organization.

 What you'll do

 Apply analytics to manufacturing’s biggest problems. Hold an evidence-backed view of what is worth the company's attention and in what order, rather than working a request list. Take the hardest two or three problems in Anduril's flagship programs and build analytics into them end to end, hands-on.

 Make the various business units in Anduril decide earlier. Shift Manufacturing reporting from retrospective to leading: risk surfaced two months before the gate, not status recited on the day of it. Adoption is the deliverable. A correct dashboard nobody opens has failed.

 Turn what worked into the enterprise standard. Generalize proven capabilities into supported products, standardize the definitions the work proved out, and consolidate the duplicated reporting they replace. A standard that survives contact with a program running at rate is defensible. One written in a document is not.

 Answer what it takes to scale. Own the analytical side of a ramp from low rate to high rate, and keep a current, evidenced view of the constraints that actually bind as the company grows.

 Build the team and the foundation. Lead the consolidated analytics organization and the managers within it. Build on and in the Manufacturing process/team rather than beside them. Hold the line that the various business units own master data quality while the analytics team builds the tooling that makes defects visible and cheap to fix.

 Your work should produce numbers the business can trust. Where a metric is known to be wrong, it is a defect with an owner and a date, not a caveat on a slide. Fix the data before building on top of it.

 Required qualifications

 10+ years in analytics, data, or quantitative operations, including 5+ years leading analytics or data teams, and experience managing managers or clear readiness to do so.

 A rigorous, teachable approach to ambiguous problems. You can describe how you decide what to work on, how you structure an analysis, how you know when you're wrong, and how you install that method in a team.

 Genuinely hands-on. Strong SQL and a modern data stack, able to get into a dataset personally, find the answer, and defend the method. This role does not succeed as pure management.

 Demonstrated ability to identify the highest-value problem in a messy operational environment and solve it analytically.

 A track record you can point at: specific operational outcomes your work caused, with the numbers, the program, and the skeptics named.

 Experience shipping analytics as supported products with real users, and retiring what they replace.

 Able to influence business unit and functional leadership peer-to-peer without authority, and to work credibly with a program team that starts out unconvinced.

 Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance. U.S. person status required per ITAR/EAR.

 Preferred qualifications

 Operational depth in manufacturing, supply chain, or planning, including fluency with routings, work orders, MRP exceptions, and cycle counts.

 Analytical ownership of a Manufacturing ramp from low rate to high rate.

 Experience building an analytics function from a scattered starting point, consolidating people, standards, and tooling that previously sat under separate owners.

 Databricks and Palantir Foundry, dimensional modeling and semantic or ontology layers.

 High-rate or high-mix manufacturing, defense Manufacturing, or another environment scaling volume fast.

 Manage and Oversee AP Operations: Lead, mentor, and develop the Accounts Payable team, ensuring all departmental tasks are executed accurately and efficiently. This includes overseeing the entire procure-to-pay cycle from invoice receipt to payment disbursement.

 Reporting and Analysis: Generate accurate and timely AP reports for management, providing insights into AP aging, vendor spend, and key performance indicators (KPIs). Analyze data to identify trends and areas for improvement.

 Team Development: Recruit, train, and manage AP staff, fostering a collaborative and high-performing team environment. Conduct performance reviews and provide ongoing feedback.

 Knowledge of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools.

 Munich, Berlin or Frankfurt

 Cloudflare is looking for a Startup Account Executive to join our Digital Natives team in Germany and Austria. You'll build your own customer base from the ground up, mostly through your own prospecting or by working closely with your BDR. Your job is to find promising startups across the region, win them early and help them build on Cloudflare as they grow.

 You'll work with AI startups, developer tool companies and other young tech businesses, often in the first years after their funding. Their teams are small, and founders make most of the decisions. Often an engineer has been using Cloudflare long before anyone talks to sales. You know this world, and you're comfortable talking about technology with a founder or CTO. You don't need to know every spec, but you understand what they're building and what Cloudflare can change for them.

 The pace is high. You'll spend a good part of your week reaching out to founders and engineers, following up and booking first meetings. You'll also build your network in the startup scene. VC firms, accelerators and founder communities are often the fastest way to the right companies, and you'll become a familiar face there. If you enjoy the hunt and like seeing your own work turn into new customers, you'll like this job.

 Above all, we are looking for true team players. We win together, not as lone wolves with sharp elbows. You share what works, ask for help when you need it, and celebrate your colleagues' wins as much as your own. You see your BDR, Solutions Engineers and specialists as real partners, not as support functions, and you bring the same care to working with your colleagues as you do to working with your customers. If you believe the best results come from people who make each other better, you'll feel right at home on our team.

 AI tools are a big part of how we sell. Many of the startups you work with are building AI products themselves, and they notice when you work the same way. We expect you to use AI every way, from researching accounts to preparing for meetings.

   Responsibilities

 Building your customer base: Find and win new startup customers across DACH, and build your book of business from the first deal. Hit or beat your quarterly targets for new customers.

 Pipeline generation: Own your pipeline from the first contact. Most of it will come from your own prospecting, such as cold outreach to founders and CTOs, LinkedIn and startup events. Your BDR supports you, but you set the pace.

 VC and accelerator relationships: Build relationships with VC firms, accelerators and startup programmes in DACH. Get to know their portfolios, find the companies where Cloudflare fits and get warm introductions to founders.

 Product-led growth: Find startups whose developers already use Cloudflare's free or self-serve plans, and turn that usage into a commercial relationship as the company grows.

 Founders and technical buyers: Have credible conversations with founders, CTOs and lead engineers about what they're building. Explain what Cloudflare changes for them, for example lower infrastructure costs or less time spent running infrastructure.

 AI startups: Position Workers AI, AI Gateway, Vectorize and R2 with startups building AI products. Understand their usual problems, such as inference costs and securing AI APIs.

 Fast sales cycles: Run short, efficient sales cycles with many deals at the same time. Follow up quickly, spend your time on the startups with the most potential and close with confidence.

 Long-term thinking: Choose startups that can grow into large customers, and set them up on Cloudflare in a way that lets them scale with us.

 Teamwork: Work closely with your BDR and Customer Engineers. Plan accounts together, bring them into conversations at the right moment and keep everyone up to date. Work with Sales Ops, Product and Customer Success to keep deals moving and get new customers off to a strong start.

 Pipeline and forecasting: Keep your pipeline in Salesforce accurate and give your manager forecasts they can rely on.

 AI in your daily work: Use AI tools every day for account research, personalised outreach, meeting prep and follow-ups. In the interview, we'll ask you how AI helps you get better results.

 Market insight: Share what you see in the DACH startup scene with the wider team, such as which funding rounds to watch and which technologies startups choose.

 Sales Experience

 2+ years in B2B technology sales with a quota, including at least one role you held for two years or more

 Met or beat your quota in your most recent full year

 Won new customers mainly through your own prospecting, such as cold email, calls and LinkedIn

 You enjoy prospecting and are used to a high volume of outreach every week

 Sold to startups or scale-ups, or worked closely with VC firms or accelerators

 Run full sales cycles with many deals at the same time

 Ideally sold to developers or CTOs before

 Worked with a structured sales method such as MEDDPICC

 Startup background

 Ideally you've worked at an AI or tech startup yourself

 You know how startups are funded (seed, Series A, Series B) and what each stage means for their budget and priorities

 You have a network in the DACH startup scene, or you know how to build one quickly

 Technical knowledge

 You can explain the basics of how the internet works: DNS, CDN, TLS, HTTP and APIs

 You know how startups typically build their products, using public cloud, serverless, open-source tools and AI APIs

 You have solid public cloud know-how. You understand how companies use AWS, GCP, Azure, including Kubernetes and serverless. What drives their cost and where Cloudflare complements or replaces them.

 You know how modern engineering teams ship software, including CI/CD and developer tooling such as GitHub, GitLab and AI coding tools like Claude Code.

 Knowing Cloudflare (Workers, R2, AI Gateway, Zero Trust) or a competitor such as AWS, Akamai, Fastly or Vercel is a plus

 Tools and ways of working

 You use Salesforce or a similar CRM every day and keep your pipeline accurate

 You've worked in a team with BDRs and pre-sales engineers

 Other

 Fluent German and English, spoken and written

 Able to travel within DACH and to startup events

title: Systems Engineer - Network Software Performance
descriptionPlain:
About Us

 At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

 At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

  Locations: Austin TX, Champaign IL, Lisbon Portugal, London England, Atlanta GA, Washington DC,

 About the team

 Cloudflare is redefining the way networks are run at scale, and some of the largest networks in the world now run their traffic through us. Cloudflare's network runs in hundreds of cities on general-purpose Linux servers, not dedicated routers, so the routers, firewalls, load balancers, and proxies that carry our customers' traffic are software that we write, ship, and operate ourselves.

 Our Packet Processing team builds and operates that software: high-performance code that processes customer traffic at the packet level as it moves through Cloudflare's network, in every Cloudflare data center. That includes the L4 load balancer at the front door of every server, a per-customer routing and forwarding data plane, a stateful network firewall, and a TCP/UDP reverse proxy (the engines behind products like Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Network Firewall, and Spectrum).

 We are a team of engineers who obsess over performance, correctness, and reliability at massive scale. We own what we build in production, a lot of our work happens close to the kernel and the NIC.

 About the role

 For us, performance is a product feature. Customers notice single-flow throughput, packet loss, and latency right away, and every CPU cycle we spend on a packet is multiplied across every server in our network. We're looking for engineers who love finding out where the time goes, and then making it go away.

 Some of the things you'd work on:

 Pushing single large flows (e.g., one tunnel carrying a customer's whole data center) to multiple Gbps and beyond, and making that performance consistent

 Finding out exactly where packets get dropped and why: NIC queues, interrupts and softirq, XDP, veth and namespaces, userspace rings, and everything in between

 CPU placement: NUMA, RSS, core isolation, and steering traffic to the right cores on servers that also run many other services

 Cutting the CPU cost per packet in hot paths written in Rust, C, and Go: batching, cache-friendly data structures, fewer copies, fewer locks

 Measuring all of it: profiling with perf, eBPF tracing, and flame graphs; continuous profiling across the fleet; benchmarks in the lab and careful experiments in production

 Building the benchmark and test tooling that keeps performance regressions from shipping

 Helping shape a unified data plane platform so that it's fast from the start

 We write mostly Go and Rust (plus C for eBPF) on Linux, and the work ranges from NIC configuration and the kernel network stack to userspace packet pipelines.

 You'll build, deploy, and operate these systems on top of one of the largest edge networks in the world. You'll partner with some of the best engineers and product managers, on our team and across Cloudflare, to solve big problems that have a meaningful impact in the lives of our customers and users.

 We're looking for curious, empathetic engineers who are excited to join us in changing the way networking is done!

 Examples of desirable skills, knowledge, and experience

 Systems programming experience in Rust, Go, C, or C++

 Performance analysis on Linux: perf, eBPF-based tracing (e.g., bpftrace, BCC), flame graphs, hardware counters

 A working model of modern CPUs and memory: caches, NUMA, branch prediction, SIMD, and how they show up in a profile

 Knowledge of how packets move through Linux: NIC queues, RSS, NAPI, GRO/GSO, softirq, and the socket layer

 Experience making high-throughput or low-latency systems faster, and proving it with good measurements

 A solid understanding of L3 and L4 networking: IP, TCP, UDP, and tunneling

 Building and operating large-scale, reliable, distributed systems

 Operating what you build: on-call, incident response, and root cause analysis

 Reading unfamiliar code and safely evolving systems that have been in production for years

 Owning work end to end, from design through deployment, and working across teams to land shared solutions

 Clear written and verbal communication; we design in written specs and review each other's work

 Bonus points

 Tuning AF_XDP, DPDK, or other kernel-bypass systems

 Low-latency backgrounds such as trading systems, HPC, games, or storage

 Go runtime or Rust async performance work

 NIC offloads and features (e.g., checksum, TSO/LRO, flow steering, SR-IOV)

 Contributions to the Linux kernel or open-source performance tooling

RDQ227R1176

 While candidates in the listed location(s) are encouraged for this role, candidates in other locations (US based) will be considered.

  Mission

 Databricks is hiring an L6 Staff Enterprise Security Engineer to expand Enterprise Security coverage across a rapidly evolving enterprise and product environment. This role will focus on securing enterprise applications, cross-system integrations, data flows, and emerging AI-adjacent use cases. The scope includes partnership with the Data team on corporate production development within the Databricks platform, through security reviews of implementation designs, hardening, configuration oversight, and broader enterprise data-security discussions, as well as modern access patterns such as MCP, integration, and trust boundary security, security automation, and broader security engineering support across enterprise platforms and services. This engineer will help identify risk, define practical security requirements, and improve security outcomes through strong technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and cross-functional partnership.

  Opportunity

 This role sits at the intersection of enterprise architecture, security engineering, product security partnership, and business enablement. Corporate production development within the Databricks platform remains owned by the Data team; EntSec defines how we engage, reviewing implementation designs, configurations, and data flows as capabilities are built, alongside ongoing enterprise application and integration reviews. The engineer will assess new technologies, integrations, and workflows with an emphasis on secure design, authentication and authorization, data handling, logging, third-party connectivity, API and token security, and operational resilience. The role partners closely with Product Engineering, IT, Legal Privacy, and business stakeholders to surface risk early, set clear requirements, and build automation that scales security coverage. This is a strong opportunity to help shape how Enterprise Security supports Databricks product development, enterprise data security, SaaS, and internal platforms, automation, and AI-connected systems as the environment continues to grow in complexity.

  Requirements

 8+ years of experience in security engineering, enterprise security, application security, cloud security, or a related field.

 Experience conducting security design or architecture reviews for product features, enterprise applications, SaaS platforms, integrations, or internally developed systems.

 Hands-on familiarity with the Databricks platform or comparable data/AI platforms (Unity Catalog, workspace governance, service principals, data access patterns).

 Strong understanding of authentication, authorization, SSO, federation, SCIM, API security, token handling, secrets management, and least privilege design.

 Experience assessing data flows, third-party integrations, trust boundaries, logging and monitoring, and security controls across interconnected systems.

 Proven track record building security automation in production: monitoring, posture checks, review workflows, or tooling (Python, SQL, Terraform, or similar).

 Ability to evaluate risk in modern enterprise environments, including automation platforms, AI-adjacent workflows, and emerging integration patterns such as MCP.

 Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate technical risk into clear requirements and actionable guidance.

 Experience driving security outcomes through engineering judgment, influence, and scalable process improvement.

 Familiarity with cloud platforms, enterprise identity systems, and core control domains such as audit logging, encryption, access control, data retention, and incident response.

  Outcomes

  OUTCOME 1:  Establish a consistent EntSec engagement model with the Data team on corporate production development within the Databricks platform: security review of implementation designs, hardening guidance, configuration oversight, and tracked remediation, while Data retains ownership of product development and delivery.

You'll join as one of the key engineers building out the Lakebase product.

LBM interacts with every Lakebase component (storage, compute, proxy, and console) and manages the full database lifecycle at scale, with a focus on reliability. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role: you lead the team technically and partner with the team's engineering manager, who owns people management and delivery planning. The stack is Go, Rust, PostgreSQL, and Kubernetes.

  The impact you will have:

 Set the technical direction for LBM and own the quality and reliability of what the team ships, driving execution on the hardest, highest-risk parts.

 Drive architecture and design, and write code on the hardest parts of your team's projects.

 Set and uphold high technical standards through architecture reviews, testing, and a culture of engineering excellence.

 Define SLIs, meet SLOs, and drive long-term reliability improvements across the database lifecycle.

 8+ years designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems, including the processes around testing, monitoring, and SLIs/SLOs.

 A track record of technical leadership as an individual contributor: setting architecture and direction for a team's projects through influence, without formal management authority.

 Strong hands-on depth: you still design systems and write production code, and can go deep on architecture for large-scale distributed services.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Enterprise Platform
descriptionPlain:
Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does:  play video games.  Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

 Discord's Enterprise Technology org is building a software engineering discipline from the ground up, and this is the founding engineering hire. There is no Enterprise Platform team yet. You will not be maintaining a status quo or joining an existing backlog: you will define the discipline, set the technical foundation, and build the platform that lets the internal systems enabling Discordians scale with the company.

 Discord's mission is to cultivate belonging, and doing that at scale requires internal systems that move as fast as the product itself. The mission of this role is to turn our enterprise infrastructure into self-service software. Your job is to replace manual consoles and tickets with a platform of reusable primitives, building blocks like "provision a device" or "push an IAM policy or app integration through code," exposed through clean APIs and self-service portals. As a code-forward Staff engineer, you will design abstractions that hide the messy reality of Okta, Jamf, and Terraform (our identity, device management, and infrastructure-as-code tools) behind interfaces people actually want to use, operating with a platform-as-a-product mindset.

  What You'll Do

 Manage the device fleet as code: Move device configuration off consoles and into versioned, API-driven infrastructure for endpoint management and hardware provisioning.

 Automate the identity layer: Manage identity systems and their connections to downstream apps as code, from SSO and SCIM integrations to account workflows, so changes ship through version control and CI/CD instead of an admin console.

 Own app delivery and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC): Build deployment pipelines and provisioning patterns that let internal systems be built and changed safely, establishing CI/CD standards.

 Build the self-service layer: Design and ship the APIs, CLIs, and portals that compose primitives into paved paths, like a new hire's first day, where software access and group memberships land in one automated, auditable flow.

 Set the foundation: Define the technical direction and architecture for the discipline, writing the RFCs and documentation that future hires will build on.

  What You Should Have

 6+ years building and operating production software and systems at a technology company, with a track record of owning ambiguous projects end to end.

 Strong software engineering fundamentals. You write production code (we lean on Python, TypeScript and Rust), and design, test, and ship it. This is not a systems admin role.

 Deep, hands-on IAM experience (SSO, SCIM, OAuth/OIDC, RBAC) and fluency with infrastructure as code (Terraform) and CI/CD.

 Experience treating endpoint and fleet management as an API-driven engineering surface at scale.

 A platform-as-a-product mindset. You have built self-service tooling that people chose to adopt.

 Comfort with ambiguity and a founder's temperament; energized by building from scratch.

  Bonus Points

 Hands-on experience with Okta, Jamf, or Intune.

 Experience with identity and access governance for non-human, workload, or AI-agent principals.

 Background at a high-growth consumer tech company with a highly technical employee base.

 Experience owning a production model end to end: the in-house versus agency versus creator call, a real budget, and the partner relationships behind it

 People leadership. You have hired, developed, and given hard feedback to producers, editors, or an external bench

 Fluency across the format spectrum, from social-first short-form to long-form storytelling, launch films, and customer narratives, with clear opinions on what each format is good for

 Improve debugging, observability, and test coverage using pytest, RSpec, and related frameworks; track and improve latency, error rates, and test coverage so AI-powered chat workflows stay reliable at scale.

 Collaborate with Product, User Experience (UX), frontend, and AI specialists to refine requirements and deliver high-quality improvements through iteration.

 Document standards, patterns, and learnings with other engineers, raising the bar for safe AI integration and evidence-driven engineering.

 Participate in Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and strengthen resiliency.

 Significant experience building and maintaining production Python backends, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous or long-running workloads.

 Working proficiency in Ruby on Rails, or a strong willingness to learn it. Duo Chat integrates deeply with the GitLab monolith for chat entry points, GraphQL, permissions, and flow registration, and most of GitLab's codebase is written in Ruby.

 Proficiency designing or extending REST or GraphQL APIs with attention to scalability, maintainability, and backward compatibility.

 Strong Structured Query Language (SQL) skills and familiarity with relational databases such as PostgreSQL, including efficient queries and data modeling.

 Ability to find, diagnose, and prevent performance and reliability problems at scale.

 Experience solving technical problems of high scope and complexity and advocating for quality, security, and performance improvements across your team.

    About the Team:

    The Interplanetary Sciences Program was   established   to expand access to scientific exploration across our solar system. Its mission is to make planetary research faster, more affordable, and more capable than ever before by rethinking how science missions are designed, built, and   operated  . The program aims to enable scientists to send instruments to distant worlds without decades of development or prohibitive costs. By creating a sustainable model for interplanetary exploration, we are transforming space science from an occasional event into a continuous process of discovery that accelerates knowledge, broadens participation, and inspires the next generation of explorers  .

    About the Role:

  Own the complete storage platform software stack for a space-based data center: custom Linux kernel drivers, OpenZFS pool design, NFS data serving, and automated fault recovery, shipping a platform that preserves up to a petabyte of mission data through years of radiation exposure

  Design and implement custom Linux kernel drivers for NVMe fault recovery and GPIO overcurrent protection, working across PCI/PCIe, block layer, and interrupt subsystems to detect and recover from radiation-induced upsets without data loss

  Lead the ZFS pool topology architectural decisions by building quantitative reliability models that balance upset probability, resilver risk, and capacity over a 6+ year mission, then validate through fault injection testing

  Develop the integration layer between NVMe controller reset and ZFS, ensuring that a drive recovering from a transient fault re-enters the storage pool cleanly, bridging driver-level recovery with filesystem-level fault tolerance

   Rapidly prototype on commodity hardware, from first boot through sustained 10 Gbps writes with automated fault recovery, de-risking the architecture before committing to the target platform, then carry the design through integration and launch

    About You:

   5+ years writing Linux kernel code, actual driver development involving PCI/PCIe devices, block storage, or interrupt-driven hardware, with meaningful time spent in kernel space

   Experience with storage systems: ZFS or other copy-on-write filesystems, RAID, NVMe internals, or high-throughput network storage (e.g., NFS)

   Depth in one or more: filesystem internals, block layer / device management, or storage protocol implementation

  Strong working knowledge of OS internals: virtual memory, interrupt context constraints, synchronization primitives, and I/O stack behavior

    Nice to haves but not required:

   Hands-on experience at the driver hardware software boundary: DMA coherency, MMIO semantics, PCIe enumeration, and cache behavior

   Strong working knowledge of data structures and systems reasoning for storage (Merkle trees, NVMe submission/completion queue ring buffers, hash tables, radix trees)

   Experience testing storage systems, including fault injection (PCIe/NVMe resets, error storms), low-level tracing (ftrace/perf/bpftrace), and crash dump analysis (kdump/vmcore)

   Experience designing software recovery around storage hardware fault cases, whether that's storage firmware, autonomous vehicle data systems, large-scale distributed infrastructure, or embedded platforms

  Familiarity with embedded Linux build systems (Yocto or Buildroot) and cross-compilation

   Hardware lab comfort: serial consoles, logic analyzers, and willingness to debug PCIe enumeration failures on a prototype board alongside the electrical engineers

title: Propulsion Responsible Engineer II, Combustion Devices
descriptionPlain:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

  Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and   technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

    About the Team:

  The Propulsion team at Relativity is focused on developing and delivering highly performant and manufacturable engines for Terran R. Engineers are responsible for the entire lifecycle of their parts, from initial design through production to qualification and flight. The team fosters a culture of bottoms-up decision-making, free from technical gatekeeping, where ownership and accountability are key at all levels. But designing engines with a quarter million pounds of thrust is just the beginning. As the flight configuration enters qualification, the team is now exploring modifications for future engines, including thrust upgrades, new cycles, and design for mass production.

   About the role:

 As a Responsible Engineer in the Combustion Devices team, you'll have cradle-to-grave ownership of an ignition system. This is ownership that covers torch igniters, ignition initiation devices, ignition system fluids design, and integration into the main combustors.

 In this role, you'll set igniter operating points, size feed circuits, own the thermal and structural analysis, release drawings, define instrumentation and sequencing for development testing, and run your own hot fires. You'll support the architecture trades for future engines and carry your system through its qualification campaign. This level of end-to-end ownership over combustion hardware is rare in the aerospace industry, where these responsibilities are typically distributed across multiple teams and organizations.

 Ignition systems interface with injectors, chambers, GSE, and avionics, requiring coordination across those disciplines and direct accountability for hardware decisions throughout the product lifecycle.

 Pyrotechnic ignition background and experience with solid motors, solid propellants, or initiators are relevant and highly welcomed.

  About you:

  Bachelor's degree in a science or engineering field

  2+ years of experience working in the development of propulsion components, combustion components, or energetic hardware

  Experience applying engineering fundamentals in fluids, thermodynamics, thermal, and structural analysis

  Working knowledge of fluid system sizing and metering, compressible and choked flow, cryogenic fluid flows, and transient behavior during valve sequencing

  Demonstrated ownership of hardware through design, build, and test

   Nice to haves:

  Master's degree in a science or engineering field

  Torch igniter, small combustor, or igniter feed system design

  Combustion devices experience: injectors, preburners, gas generators, augmenters, or thrust chambers

  Solid propulsion background: motor and grain design, solid propellants, pyrotechnic initiators, or energetics handling

  Experience in a rocket engine development and/or test environment

  Transient fluid network modeling, CFD, or thermostructural FEA

  Valve or flow control component design

  Clear evidence of ownership from school or work experience

title: Principal Algorithm Engineer (EO/IR Image Analysis)
descriptionPlain:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

 Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

  SPACE SYSTEMS

 Rocket Lab’s Space Systems division builds complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space including solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, and radios.

 The Space Systems division has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. We have built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help get to space — our Space Systems division is empowering the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

  PRINCIPAL ALGORITHM ENGINEER - (EO/IR IMAGE ANALYSIS)

 Rocket Lab Optical Systems solves mission-critical space domain and Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance challenges for Department of Defense and Intelligence Community customers. Our vision is to revolutionize the space-based payload market with innovative and novel designs for space, terrestrial, and airborne environments. Building on more than 20 years of electro-optical and infrared systems innovation from Geost, Rocket Lab Optical Systems delivers solutions to the warfighter for responsive, scalable sensing solutions across all orbital domains.

 As a Principal Algorithm Engineer for Rocket Lab Optical Systems in Long Beach, CA, you will develop, validate, and deploy advanced algorithms for advanced EO/IR space payloads, with an emphasis on image processing, object detection, and tracking. You will collaborate with multidisciplinary teams in machine learning, optical design, and space vehicle modeling and simulation as well as design and protype processing claims for next-generation space payloads.

  WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO

 Develop, optimize, and validate complex EO/IR image-processing chains and support their deployment into real-time implementations on space-based sensor payloads.

 Bring your understanding of the physics of optical sensors and image formation to develop and optimize modeling and simulation frameworks to simulation mission imagery.

 Use these simulation frameworks to synthesize mission imagery to support machine learning training and image algorithm validation.

 Apply classical and modern (deep learning) approaches to detect and track low-SNR objects within EO/IR imagery for mission-critical applications.

 Work with software and firmware teams to transition complex image-processing algorithms into high-performance, real-time implementations.

 Support and enhance existing operational programs, including maintaining and improving deployed algorithms, troubleshooting fielded systems, and ensuring ongoing system performance and reliability.

 Analyze large and complex EO/IR datasets to extract analytics and assess algorithm performance.

 Document and present algorithm performance results to technical and non-technical stakeholders, including government customers.

 Attend technical interchange meetings and represent the organization in matters pertaining to project development.

 Support travel or off-site work, as needed.

 Bachelor's degree with 12+ years of experience, master's degree with 8+ years of experience, or Ph.D. with 5+ years of experience in physics, optical sciences, computer science, mathematics, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related technical discipline with demonstrated experience in image processing or EO/IR systems.

 Strong experience in designing, implementing, testing, and optimizing image processing and computer vision algorithms for EO/IR sensors.

 Broad experience in areas of computer vision, such as image stabilization/registration, 3-D multi-view camera modeling, pose reconstruction (bundle adjustment), object detection and tracking, and background suppression.

 Proficiency in Python with strong programming skills.

 Demonstrated experience image-system modeling and simulation.

 Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document technical work and present results to diverse audiences.

 Ability to contribute to a high-performance team.

 Leadership skills supporting the completion of program and project milestones.

 S. citizenship is required due to program requirements.

 Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government Security Clearance.

 Strong math background, particularly linear algebra.

 Experience with modern, deep-learning-based approaches to computer vision.

 Experience with space-looking or space-based imaging systems.

 Experience with sensor calibration procedures (radiometric, geometric, temporal) for EO/IR systems.

 Proficiency in C/C++

 Experience across all phases of product development, including proposal design architectures, requirements generation, design development, integration, verification, and transition to production.

 Every launch starts with a question: will it hold? As a Dynamics & Structural Analyst at Rocket Lab, you'll answer it. Using modelling, simulation, and real flight data, you'll predict the violent vibration, shock, and loads that Electron endures from the pad to orbit and prove our structures can take it. From FEA that optimises dynamic response to post-processing flight data that validates every prediction, your analysis is what turns bold designs into reliable launch vehicles.   SENIOR TEST ENGINEER I

 Rocket Lab Robotics specializes in high-performance robotic systems and precision mechanisms that enable the most ambitious space missions, including NASA’s Mars Perseverance Rover and CADRE lunar rovers. Leveraging Mars-proven expertise from Motiv Space Systems, we deliver scalable, flight-proven solutions – such as robotic arms, motion control systems, and solar array drive assemblies (SADAs) – to support planetary exploration, satellite servicing, and national security missions.

 Rocket Lab Robotics is seeking an experienced Senior Test Engineer I to support the development, qualification, and production of advanced spaceflight hardware, including robotic systems, precision electromechanical mechanisms, motion control electronics, optomechanical assemblies, and other high-reliability spacecraft components.

 The Senior Test Engineer I is responsible for developing, implementing, validating, and maintaining test systems, equipment, procedures, and supporting software used to verify the functional performance and compliance of complex aerospace hardware.This position works closely with Systems Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, and Production to translate product requirements into effective, repeatable test methods and manufacturing test capabilities.The successful candidate will combine strong electrical and electromechanical engineering experience with proficiency in instrumentation, test automation, data acquisition, hardware troubleshooting, and engineering verification practices. The position requires the ability to independently develop and execute complex test engineering solutions in a high-mix, low-volume aerospace manufacturing environment.

  WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO:

  Test Engineering and Development

 Develop and implement test strategies, methods, procedures, and equipment supporting development, qualification, and acceptance testing of spaceflight hardware.

 Translate engineering specifications and verification requirements into executable test procedures, measurement methods, and acceptance criteria.

 Design and develop test systems for robotic mechanisms, electromechanical actuators, motor controllers, sensors, and associated electronic hardware.

 Establish test configurations, measurement requirements, instrumentation selection, and data acquisition methods.

 Develop repeatable test processes appropriate for prototype, qualification, and flight hardware.

 Collaborate with Systems Engineering and Design Engineering to ensure test methods adequately address applicable product requirements.

 Participate in technical design reviews, test readiness reviews, and verification planning activities.

 Identify testability constraints and recommend improvements to product design, interfaces, and verification methods.

  Test Equipment and Automation

 Design, develop, implement, and maintain automated and manual test equipment for complex aerospace hardware.

 Develop electrical and mechanical test fixtures, interface assemblies, instrumentation configurations, and supporting test infrastructure.

 Create and maintain test automation software using Python, LabVIEW, MATLAB, or other applicable development environments.

 Integrate sensors, transducers, data acquisition systems, power supplies, electronic loads, motion controllers, and other instrumentation into test systems.

 Develop test software for equipment control, data collection, automated sequencing, and results processing.

 Establish and document test equipment calibration, verification, maintenance, and configuration requirements.

 Troubleshoot test equipment, instrumentation, software, and communication interface issues.

 Improve test system reliability, measurement accuracy, repeatability, and operational efficiency.

 Support development of reusable test equipment and automation capabilities across multiple product lines.

  Hardware Verification and Testing

 Identify test anomalies, measurement discrepancies, and hardware performance issues.

 Coordinate with Systems Engineering and Design Engineering to resolve technical discrepancies and verification concerns.

 Support engineering investigations, qualification activities, and flight hardware acceptance processes.

 Analyze electrical signals, mechanical behavior, control system responses, and test data to identify potential failure mechanisms.

 Troubleshoot electrical, electronic, mechanical, and electromechanical systems using engineering documentation and appropriate instrumentation.

 Collaborate with Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality Assurance, and Production personnel to identify root causes and corrective actions.

 Evaluate test anomalies to distinguish hardware failures from test equipment, instrumentation, or procedural issues.

 Develop and implement approved improvements to test equipment, procedures, and measurement methods.

 Support nonconformance investigations, corrective action activities, and verification of corrective action effectiveness.

 Document technical findings, test anomalies, and recommended engineering solutions.

 Ensure test procedures clearly define test configurations, equipment requirements, execution steps, measurement methods, and acceptance criteria.

 Develop test data collection, reporting, and analysis methods appropriate for applicable product requirements.

 Maintain test equipment documentation, software configuration records, calibration requirements, and test system design data.

 Support controlled release and revision of test procedures and engineering documentation.

 Ensure test processes and documentation comply with applicable configuration management, quality, and contractual requirements.

 Review test results and support preparation of engineering verification reports, qualification reports, and acceptance data packages.

 Support traceability between product requirements, verification activities, and test evidence.

 Provide test engineering support to manufacturing technicians performing integration, functional testing, and acceptance testing.

 Support deployment, validation, and maintenance of production test equipment and automated test systems.

 Troubleshoot test-related manufacturing issues and identify opportunities to improve testing efficiency.

 Collaborate with Manufacturing Engineering to develop testable, repeatable manufacturing processes.

 Support technician training on test equipment operation, test procedures, and troubleshooting methods.

 Coordinate with Production and Production Control to address test equipment availability, technical constraints, and manufacturing readiness.

 Support new product introduction and transition of engineering test methods into controlled production test processes.

 Identify opportunities to reduce test cycle time, equipment downtime, and recurring test issues.

 Ensure test engineering activities comply with applicable aerospace quality, customer, and contractual requirements.

 Collaborate with Quality Assurance to establish appropriate test verification methods, documentation requirements, and product acceptance processes.

 Support investigation and resolution of test failures, nonconformances, and product quality issues.

 Ensure test equipment, procedures, and software are maintained under appropriate configuration control.

 Establish appropriate calibration and measurement traceability requirements for test equipment and instrumentation.

 Participate in test readiness reviews, quality audits, and technical compliance assessments as required.

 Promote disciplined test execution, accurate documentation, and protection of high-value flight hardware.

 Identify opportunities to improve test automation, measurement accuracy, equipment reliability, and test efficiency.

 Develop reusable test software, equipment architectures, fixtures, and procedures across product lines.

 Support standardization of test engineering methods and practices within the organization.

 Provide technical guidance and mentorship to less-experienced engineers and test technicians.

 Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related technical discipline.

 Demonstrated experience developing test systems, procedures, and equipment for complex electrical, mechanical, or electromechanical hardware.

title: Legal Fellow - Human Frontier Collective
descriptionPlain:
The  Human Frontier Collective (HFC) ’s mission is to bring the world's best minds to shape the future of AI – because the future of AI depends not only on powerful models, but on the people who teach them to think. We bring together researchers, academics, and domain leaders across 70+ fields – over 90% of members hold doctorates – to shape how frontier AI systems are built, evaluated, and governed. HFC members have since co-authored published work including   SciPredict  ,   PropensityBench  , and   Professional Reasoning Benchmark .

 Why join the HFC

 HFC centers on three core pillars: the network itself, participation in selected AI/ML projects, and opportunities to publish with our research team.

  Join a unique and exclusive expert network:  You’ll become a part of an interdisciplinary community, consisting of over 90% doctorates and field leaders representing 70+ fields from the leading institutions. We’re a collective of top innovators and thought leaders committed to advancing frontier AI to power the world’s most important decisions.

  Participate in AI/ML projects:  Beyond the collective network, you’ll be regularly invited to work on high-impact projects with Scale AI and its affiliated lab and platform: building AI safety and policy guardrails, helping models understand real-world deep learning workflows by designing, reviewing, and optimizing PyTorch models, evaluating complex ML code and AI-generated implementations for efficiency and correctness, and more.

  Co-author selected research publications:  Collaborate with Scale’s research team to co-author technical reports and research papers—boosting your academic visibility and professional recognition.

  Who Should Apply

  Education:  JD, LLM, or currently enrolled in a prestigious 2L/3L program.

  Certifications:  Bar admission in any jurisdiction strongly preferred.

  Professional Background:  Experience as Attorney/Associate, Legal Analyst, Counsel, Law Clerk, In-House Counsel, Legal Researcher, or Law Professor.

  Skills:  Demonstrated expertise in legal research, analysis of regulatory frameworks, constitutional law, case law interpretation, and drafting legal briefs.

  Professional Mindset:  Detail-oriented, innovative thinker with a passion for financial technology and a commitment to collaboration. Prior experience with AI is not required, but a plus.

 How it works

  Duration : This is a fully remote opportunity with no fixed end date; engagements continue as long as there's mutual interest. This is a 1099 independent contractor engagement.

  Work authorization : We do not sponsor visas for Fellows. To participate in the HFC Fellows program, you need to have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the country you reside in.

  Community Network : Once you’ve received an invitation to join the HFC, you’ll also gain access to our newsletters, discussion channels, virtual sessions, IRL events, and much more.

  Projects Logistics :

 Project selection: You’ll regularly get matched to carefully selected projects from our partners. Depending on the partner, projects range from evaluating AI models to designing experiments, building RL environments, co-authoring research papers, and more.

 Flexible schedule: There's no minimum commitment – you decide whether to take on a project. Most fellows spend 10–25 hours per week, on a schedule they set themselves.

 Competitive pay: Project pay rates vary across platforms and depend on a number of factors, including but not limited to: projects, scope, skillset, and location. You’ll receive the pay information upon receiving project matching notifications.

 Application process

  Apply:  We review applications on a rolling basis.

  Interview:  Candidates will get to discuss their research experience, professional background, and alignment with our mission to advance human-centered AI.   Note: If we invited you directly, your invitation will say whether this step applies.

  Join the Collective:  Successful candidates will receive an invitation to join the Human Frontier Collective Fellowship.

     PLEASE NOTE:    Our policy requires a 90-day waiting period before reconsidering candidates for the same role. This allows us to ensure a fair and thorough evaluation of all applicants.

  About Us:

  At Scale, our mission is to develop reliable AI systems for the world's most important decisions. Our products provide the high-quality data and full-stack technologies that power the world's leading models, and help enterprises and governments build, deploy, and oversee AI applications that deliver real impact. We work closely with industry leaders like Meta,   Ernst     &   Young, Mayo Clinic, Time Inc., the Government of Qatar, and U.S. government agencies including the Army and Air Force. We are expanding our team to accelerate the development of AI applications.

  We believe that everyone should be able to bring their whole selves to work, which is why we are proud to be an inclusive and equal opportunity workplace. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability status, gender identity or Veteran status.

  We are committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with physical and mental disabilities. If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation in the application or recruiting process due to a disability, please contact us at accommodations@scale.com. Please see the United States Department of Labor's    Know Your Rights poster    for additional information.

  We comply with the United States Department of Labor's   Pay Transparency provision  .

   PLEASE NOTE:  We collect, retain and use personal data for our professional business purposes, including notifying you of job opportunities that may be of interest and sharing with our affiliates. We limit the personal data we collect to that which we believe is appropriate and necessary to manage applicants’ needs, provide our services, and comply with applicable laws. Any information we collect in connection with your application will be treated in accordance with our internal policies and programs designed to protect personal data. Please see our  privacy policy  for additional information.

title: Frontier Data Strategist
descriptionPlain:
Frontier AI labs decide what direction their models need to take before the actual training starts. As a Frontier Data Strategist on Scale's Generative AI team, you'll be a trusted voice in those decisions. You'll partner with research leads and senior stakeholders at the world's leading AI labs to shape the data strategy behind their next generation of models, then design the human-data programs to deliver it.

 You'll sit where frontier research meets Scale's product roadmap, and you'll be expected to move both. With customers, you'll own senior, technically grounded relationships, anticipate where their research is heading, and bring them new data ideas before they ask. Inside Scale, you'll be a leading voice with our AI Product Managers, ML Research, Delivery Operations, and Engagement Management teams, turning what you learn from customers into product priorities and investment decisions.

 This is a forward-looking, highly cross-functional role. Our Engagement Managers own customer success for live programs; Frontier Data Strategists own everything that comes before it: spotting the need, designing the program, scoping and forecasting it, and winning the work. As a senior member of the team, you'll set the standard for how Scale does this work and help develop the Frontier Data Strategists around you.

  What you’ll do:

 Own relationships with senior research stakeholders at your assigned frontier labs, such as research leads, heads of post-training, and technical leadership, and become a strategic thought partner on their post-training, evaluation, and agent roadmaps.

 Set the data strategy for your accounts: anticipate needs across research areas, spot where the biggest opportunities are, and build a multi-program plan for how Scale can help.

 Direct the cross-functional team designing Scale's most complex and novel human-data programs, including work that has no precedent at Scale.

 Shape Scale's product roadmap by representing your customers in planning with AI Product Managers and ML Research, and by resolving tradeoffs between customer needs and what Scale can build.

 Bring insights from the frontier (research directions, emerging data needs, capability gaps) back to Scale's leadership and technical teams to guide strategy and investment decisions.

 Own the pipeline of new opportunities for your accounts. Lead scoping, forecasting, and pricing with Delivery, Growth Operations, and Finance, and see the work through to signed programs and a clean handoff.

 Mentor Frontier Data Strategists, set the bar for program design and customer engagement, and help build the playbooks the team runs on.

  What we’re looking for:

 3+ years in a technical AI/ML role, such as ML engineering, research, applied science, technical product management, or post-training data work at a lab or data provider.

 Deep fluency in the LLM training lifecycle, especially post-training: SFT, preference data, reward modeling, RL environments, evaluations, agentic training, etc.

 A track record of owning relationships with senior technical stakeholders, and of influencing their direction through substance.

 Evidence of shipping ambiguous, high-stakes technical programs from idea to delivery.

 Experience influencing a product or research roadmap without direct authority.

 The ability to read a research paper and form an opinion on what data would improve a given capability, and to defend that opinion to researchers.

 A degree in CS, engineering, math, physics, or another quantitative field.

  Ideally you'd have:

 Hands-on experience designing training data, evals, or RL environments.

 A graduate degree (PhD, MS) or published research in ML or a related field.

 Experience at a frontier lab, model developer, or AI data company.

 Experience mentoring or leading technical teammates, formally or informally.

title: Manufacturing Engineer (Falcon & Dragon)
descriptionPlain:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

  MANUFACTURING ENGINEER (FALCON & DRAGON)

 As a Manufacturing Engineer at SpaceX, you will have the opportunity to utilize your knowledge, experience, and creativity to develop novel solutions at the cutting edge of space technology. You will work on launch vehicles and spacecraft that deliver satellites into Earth's orbit, ferry humans to and from the International Space Station, and ultimately extend humanity’s reach beyond the Earth and moon. You will be a vital part of the relationship between our development and production teams. You will provide input into the design and development of new and existing hardware and take a lead role in manufacturing and integration on our current and next-generation vehicles.

  RESPONSIBILITIES:

 Responsible for the build and inspection process for the structural assembly, propulsion assembly, and integration of the Falcon & Dragon vehicles

 Develop, qualify, and refine manufacturing processes to meet all design and business requirements, including safety, quality, efficiency, and delivery

 Collaborate with other engineers, subject matter experts, and technicians to solve large-scale production challenges

 Work with design engineers to evaluate designs for manufacturability and implementation in a rapidly evolving production environment

 Resolve product non-conformances and collaborate with the quality team to implement root cause corrective actions

 Identify, plan, and execute capital equipment, machine, and layout upgrades to meet volume production demand

 Develop and refine floor layouts, capacity models, and product flow analysis to ensure on-time vehicle delivery to manifest

  BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

 Bachelor's degree in mechanical, manufacturing, aerospace, materials or industrial engineering

 1+ years of engineering experience in manufacturing or production (internship and school projects experience qualifies)

  PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

 Master’s degree in mechanical, manufacturing, aerospace, materials or industrial engineering

 Involvement in a professional engineering society or collegiate design project

 Experience with the build, assembly, or integration of large mechanical assemblies

 Knowledge of metallic manufacturing techniques, processes, and equipment related to welding, metal forming, fastening, drilling, bonding and automation

 Mechanical component and/or tooling design and analysis experience using 3D CAD software

 Experience with design for manufacture and assembly (DFMA)

 Experience transition complex products from R&D to high-volume manufacturing in a fast-paced environment

 Experience writing work instructions and procedures for critical aerospace parts

 Experience in a production environment within the aerospace industry

  ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

 Willing to work extended hours and/or weekends as needed

descriptionPlain:

We are finance transformation and AI experts working side-by-side with Finance, Product, and Engineering teams to redefine processes and build the finance organization of the future. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys working across disciplines: part solution developer, part data architect, part workflow designer, and part coach. You’ll have room to shape how applied AI is built and scaled both from a technical and end-user perspective.

  What you’ll do

 You'll work side-by-side with Finance subject matter experts to understand how work gets done, identify the highest impact opportunities, and partner with domain teams to chart a transformation plan which balances future ambitions with rapid impact.  You'll work independently to automate manual processes, design and build agents and required data solutions using internal platforms, and enable Finance teams to maintain these solutions long-term.

 You’ll build with your partner teams, not simply deliver solutions to them. You’ll help colleagues move from a manual workflow, to a first AI-enabled win, to a reliable solution they can confidently operate and improve themselves. Success means the workflow stays transformed after the initial build, the team trusts the output, and the people closest to the process can own what comes next.

 You’ll favor learning through building. When possible, you’ll put a useful prototype in front of a Finance user, test it against a real deliverable, and improve it quickly rather than spend weeks describing a theoretical future state. When you encounter platform limitations—which you will—you’ll find creative, supportable approaches, collaborate with Engineering to scope and test custom tools, and escalate strategically when needed.

 This role requires a blend of process automation, data operations, technical problem-solving, and stakeholder enablement. You'll spend your time building agents, optimizing data pipelines that feed them, creating knowledge layers that make them more accurate, and training Finance teams to use and maintain them. Success means Finance teams can independently run agents you've built while you provide light support and focus on the next automation opportunity.

  Responsibilities

 Embed with Finance teams to diagnose workflows, identify high-leverage opportunities, and translate business, data, and control requirements into practical AI and automation solutions.

 Build and operationalize AI agents for Finance use cases, delivering end-to-end solutions from prototype through validation, monitoring, documentation, and handoff.

 Write and optimize SQL for data extraction, transformation, calculation, and validation, ensuring Finance-facing outputs are accurate, explainable, and reliable.

 Design reusable knowledge layers, evaluation methods, validation patterns, data-quality frameworks, and components that improve agent accuracy and accelerate future use cases.

 Identify agentic limitations and new possibilities; determine when to use existing capabilities, develop an alternative approach, or partner with Engineering to scope and test custom tools and integrations, including tools using Model Context Protocol where appropriate.

title: Engineering Manager, Infrastructure (Privy)
descriptionPlain:
Who we are

  About Privy

 Our mission is to make privacy and user ownership the default online. To do so, we build simple, flexible APIs and tools for developers that make it easy to build new products on crypto rails.

 Privy owns the abstractions and infrastructure layer above wallets, integrating across chains, third-party providers, and Stripe products like Treasury and Link. We get to solve hard technical problems while leveraging Stripe's distribution to reach customers like Ramp, Klarna, Deel, Kraken, Hyperliquid, and Fomo — powering experiences for both mainstream users and crypto natives.

  About the team

 Engineering at Privy is distinguished by:

 High urgency—Shipping very small iterations, very fast, to learn very quickly.

 Product taste—Our customers  are  developers, and to build effective products for them requires technical knowledge —you will often be "the PM".

 Security mindset—A great portion of our product is trust. While we have a dedicated security team, every engineer brings security to their designs from the start.

 In practice, we use  boring technology  like Node, React, and AWS so we can focus our engineering energy entirely on pushing the boundaries of Privy's core product, e.g. through hardware enclaves, multi-region low-latency APIs, and blockchain abstractions that are accessible to mainstream developers.

 As an Engineering Manager at Privy, you will lead, grow, and shape high-performing engineering teams that make a massive impact on our product and industry. Your North Star is to enable and drive towards the success of Privy’s business overall.

 As the Engineering Manager of your team, the buck stops with you: you are the owner of your team’s ultimate impact on Privy’s product and business. We believe that excellence in management is why our team loves working at Privy. Incredible managers are the core driver behind Privy’s long-term success: they are force multipliers, performance coaches, culture-carriers. They build the scaffolding that supports the team and each individual’s greatest impact. They shape Privy to be the place where each person gets to do the very best work of their careers.

 We wake up every day driven to show up for our team. We shape roles around the unique strengths of every person and we are deeply grateful for the time we spend together building something greater than ourselves.

 Infrastructure at Privy is fundamentally a product. With both internal engineers (and increasingly non-engineers) as direct consumers of infra platforms, as well as external product offerings, it is essential that the infra team creates powerful abstractions, educates and grows the Privy team on shipping ever-better software, and operates deeply efficient tooling to be the lever arm for which Privy moves the world.

  What you’ll do

 Own long-term team outcomes and success of Privy’s product and business

 Drive the future vision of infrastructure of Privy alongside talented infrastructure engineers, across complex, cutting edge technology like secure enclaves (TEEs) and one-click Bring Your Own Cloud deployments, with performance and high scale as a default.

 Hold the team accountable to excellence in quality, throughput, and performance

 Leading active infrastructure work across the breadth of the company, from service definition, to reliability engineering, to developer tooling, and more

 Ensure the team is working on the right scope of work and projects, align decisions with business impact, and build interfaces with other parts of the org

 Fill gaps as a player-coach; review PRs, write and review design docs, investigate incidents – stay close to the metal and reinforce our builder culture

 Coach engineers towards growth and their career goals

 Build a supportive, fun, motivating, celebratory team culture so that the team wins every week

  Who You Are

 Deep ownership and a high-level perspective on driving overall business impact

 Performance-oriented mindset, with a high bar for quality and excellence

 Technical excellence to be able to independently evaluate quality and technical feedback

 High emotional maturity, insightfulness, and care

 Strong past experience as a manager and leader – excellent management takes reps

 Experience with any of the following a plus:

 Designing and operating systems supporting hundreds of millions of users

 Secure enclave platforms, like AWS Nitro Enclaves

 Observability, incident response, capacity planning, performance tuning, and infrastructure automation (IaC, CI/CD for infra)

 Background in building low-latency, high-throughput systems for trading or payment processing

 Any blend of public cloud/BYOC architectures

 Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

  What We're About

 At its core, this role is about uncovering dots and—without knowing the shape they form—figuring out how to connect them. Our customers come to us with a hunch that the only way to protect their troops, manufacture high-quality products, structure effective healthcare policies, or deliver aid to refugees safely is to make better use of their data. Deployment Strategists are responsible for turning that hunch into reality.

 If you believe in the transformational power of data and technology and in your own ability to bring that power to bear against complex problems, we want to meet you.

  What We Do

 As a Deployment Strategist, you'll work as part of a driven and creative team of Engineers, Product Designers, and other Deployment Strategists to deploy software against the most challenging problems our world faces. Your mission is to synthesize disconnected streams of thought into a cohesive understanding of what the most important problem is, what the data means, what the product needs, what users are motivated by, and where the impact could be.

 Deployment Strategists are do-ers who immerse themselves in our customers' most intricate workflows, partner with customer teams and explore the data, and dive into the product landscape to enable us to scale. A select number of Deployments Strategists may also be deployed to Palantir internal teams and problems. In this role, the problems you'll tackle will require a curious and analytical mindset, a sharp intuition for product, and a strong degree of user empathy to ultimately empower our customers to make better decisions.

 No two days are the same, but as a Deployment Strategist you can expect to:
  Go onsite and meet with customer analysts to understand the critical questions they need to answer and locate their biggest pain points.

 Identify relevant datasets through deep engagement with customer problems and workflows, and work with Forward Deployed Engineers to integrate the data into a stable and extensible pipeline.

 Work with the customer to build bespoke workflows for new user groups.

 Lead training sessions to ensure that the product is meeting user needs, and to ensure it is being used widely enough to have concrete impact on our partners' operations.

 Embed with our Software Engineering and Product Design teams to incorporate what you saw in the field into cross-Palantir product offerings.

 Build and deliver demos to new and existing customers.

This position requires a combination of project management, process optimisation, and execution skills. You are a person who loves fixing problems and always embraces the best idea, even when it is not your own.

 Core Responsibilities
